title: Elegbeleye lauds President Tinubu on Pedro’s Appointment
content:
Chairman of the Nigeria Premier Football League (NPFL), Otunba Gbenga Elegbeleye, has praised President Bola Ahmed Tinubu for appointing Rotimi Pedro as the new Director-General of the Nigeria Television Authority (NTA), describing the decision as a major boost for sports broadcasting in the country.

Elegbeleye said Pedro has been one of the prime advocates of commercial broadcasts in the country, which he has done for decades through his OSMI Sports marketing firm.

“I must commend the vision of Mr. President who has continued to energise the country’s socio-economic space in Nigeria through policies and appointments that has compliments his renewed hope agenda.

“Television is a very important component in the plan to build the sports economy and we, at the NPFL are very enthused as we plan to collaborate with the government broadcast agency to take the matches to homes of Nigerians through their expansive network.

“We are really excited because over the seasons, we have struggled to partner NTA to have our matches on free-to-air platforms,” he said.

Pedro has been the Chief Executive Officer of OSMI, a company that has been partnering broadcast organisations in the acquisition of television rights to major global sporting events including the Olympic Games, FIFA World Cup and CAF Nations Cup amongst others.

title: UK Seek To Strengthen Trade Ties With Nigeria, Hail Tinubu Economic Reforms
content:
The United Kingdom High Commissioner to Nigeria, Richard Montgomery, during a courtesy visit to the First Lady, Senator RemiTinubu, at the State House, Abuja, on Monday, has applauded President Bola Tinubu’s economic reforms, describing them as bold steps towards creating new opportunities for growth and stronger trade partnerships.

He said: “The UK government viewed Nigeria’s ongoing reforms as ‘difficult but necessary’ measures that were already reshaping the economic landscape. The policies have opened doors for enhanced trade relations between the two countries.

“We see a lot of positivity in Nigeria’s economy, particularly new opportunities being created by the reforms undertaken by President Tinubu.”

In her response, Senator Remi Tinubu assured her guests that the government and the Renewed Hope Initiative (the First Lady’s flagship programme, for its impact in education, health, and humanitarian services) would continue to align efforts with the Renewed Hope Agenda of President Tinubu to address challenges facing Nigerians.

title: 2026 Hajj Exercise: Intending Muslim Pilgrims Asks To Deposit N8.5m
content:
Federal Capital Territory (FCT) Muslim Pilgrims Welfare Board, through it director, Alhaji Kadiri Edah, has commenced during a meeting in Abuja, that the prospective pilgrims must deposit a minimum of N8.5 million to secure a seat for the 2026 Hajj exercise.

He said: “Intending pilgrims who wish to participate in the 2026 Hajj through the board are required to make an initial deposit of N8.5 million via a bank draft from any commercial bank, payable to the FCT Muslim Pilgrims Welfare Board, Abuja.

“We will only accept bank drafts; no cash payments will be entertained. Registration is strictly on a first-come, first-served basis to ensure fairness to all residents.

“The Board is committed to improving services for registered pilgrims through new strategies introduced for the upcoming Hajj.

 “We urge pilgrims to transact directly with the Board and avoid any fraudulent demands for extra payments outside the approved fare.”

title: 2026 World Cup Qualifiers: Super Eagles Suffer Setback With Player Ruled Out
content:
Nigeria’s preparation for the 2026 FIFA World Cup qualifiers games against Rwanda’s Amavubi and South Africa’s Bafana Bafana in September has been dealt with a major blow with Hull City defender Semi Ajayi ruled out through injury, BSNSports.com.ng reports.

Ajayi, 31-year-old, sustained the injury during Hull City’s Championship encounter against Coventry City last weekend and will be sideline in the crucial qualifiers fixtures.

According to the Hull Daily Mail, Ajayi is expected to be sidelined for between four and six weeks.

The setback comes after a difficult spell for the former West Bromwich Albion defender, who managed just 15 appearances in his final season with the Baggies.

title: Women’s Champions League Qualifier: CAF Unveils Fixture Schedule For WAFU B
content:
The West African Football Union (WAFU) Zone B in its official fixture schedule released for the upcoming CAF Women’s Champions League qualifier on Thursday, has saw Nigeria’s champions Bayelsa Queens in a challenging Group B along with Ghana’s Police Ladies, AS Garde of Niger, and Benin’s Sam Nelly FC.

Group A features Ivorian giants ASEC Mimosas, AS GNN of Niger, and Burkina Faso’s USFA.

According to the schedule, the tournament will kick off on August 23 with ASEC Mimosas taking on AS GNN in the opening game, while Bayelsa Queens begin their campaign against Police Ladies later that day.

The group stage concludes on August 30, followed by the semifinals on September 2. The third-place playoff and the grand finale are slated for September 5.

title: Nigeria’s D’Tigers Face Indomitable Lions Of Cameroon In Battle Of Beasts Showdown For Quarterfinal
content:
The 2025 AfroBasket Group B is about to witness its biggest showdown as both the unbeaten teams, Nigeria’s D’Tigers and Cameroon’s Indomitable Lions in the ongoing tournament lock horns on Sunday afternoon in Luanda for quarterfinal ticket.

Nigeria is topping the table on points difference. The stakes could not be higher, as a victory for either side secures an automatic quarterfinal ticket, while the loser will be forced to take the longer route through the playoffs.

Nigeria opened their campaign with authority, dispatching Madagascar 77-59 with swag and poise. Caleb Agada’s brilliance shone through as the D’Tigers turned a slim halftime lead into a dominant second-half display. Followed by an emphatic 87-66 win over Tunisia, ending the defending champions’ hopes of a clean sweep in Group B. Josh Okogie’s performance (33 points) in that game not only energized the squad but also signaled that Nigeria may be peaking at the right time.

With depth across positions, a versatile bench, and the ability to switch gears mid-game, the D’Tigers have shown they are not just here to compete but to reclaim glory. A win against Cameroon would send a powerful message to the rest of the field that Nigeria is a front-runner for the title they last won a decade ago.

On the other hand, Cameroon has stunned. The Lions roared into AfroBasket 2025 with a commanding 86-65 victory over defending champions Tunisia, ending the North Africans’ remarkable decade-long unbeaten run in the tournament. Williams Narace led with 20 points, while Jeremiah Hill, Yves Missi, and Fabian Ateba provided vital support.

Cameroon’s squad is buoyed by the presence of three NBA players, namely Yves Missi and Ulrich Chomche of the New Orleans Pelicans and Christian Koloko of the LA Lakers, marking a resurgence of Cameroonian basketball at the continental stage.

Their second game tested their resolve, as they narrowly escaped a Madagascar upset, edging 80-77 thanks to Jeremiah Hill’s late-game heroics. That result kept their record unblemished but also exposed areas they must tighten against a stronger Nigerian side.

Sunday’s matchup is more than just a group-stage clash, but it’s a battle for supremacy. Both teams know that finishing top of Group B guarantees direct passage to the quarterfinals, avoiding the uncertainties of the playoff round.

For Nigeria, it’s about maintaining momentum and asserting dominance and repeating the championship winning performances of 2015, ten years after.

title: FIBA: D'Tigress Top 10 Spot In The Latest FIBA World Rankings
content:
Nigeria's D'Tigress in the latest FIBA Women’s world rankings have been ranked the 8th best women's basketball team in the world and 1st in Africa. This follows their most recent fifth consecutive victory at the just concluded 2025 AfroBasket.

The win make it the Women's AfroBasket title a record seven times champions for D'Tigress and fifth consecutive victory.

D'Tigress' dominance in African women's basketball is unparalleled, and they also qualified for the 2026 FIBA Women's World Cup. 

Elsewhere, Great Britain dropped two places to 22nd while Belgium reached the top five following their EuroBasketWomen win.

South Sudan is the biggest climber as it jumped 31 spots to 55th, while the USA, as expected, continues to top the rankings.

title: Team Nigeria dominant on opening day of African Youth Scrabble Championships
content:
Team Nigeria is dictating the pace at the second edition of the Pan African Youth Scrabble Championships which started Thursday in Kenya with 138 players competing for honours in two categories.

Abdulqudus Aliu, is leading the cast of 54 players in the U-19 category with 5 wins from five games and a healthy cumulative point of plus 915. Another Nigerian, Prestige Archibong is one win away from Abdulqudus Aliu, however, Archibong has a massive cumulative point of 1244 points from 4 wins.

Home boy, Caxton Mwai, has 521 cumulative points from 5 Victories to seat behind Abdulqudus Aliu.

Joy Nwabuzor, the only Nigerian girl in the U-19 category is giving the other gender a run for their stay , with 4 wins and plus 546 points. Team captain Sufyan Olojoku is not far off the leader board with 3 wins.

In the U-15 event, Hassan from the Olojoku scrabble dynasty, Sophia Ekeruche and Eliana Igbe are just too strong for the 84 man field in the competition as they won their first 3 rounds of games with an impressive cumulative of plus 687 points for Hassan Olojoku and Sophia Ekeruche while Eliana Igbe 43 points less.

Meanwhile, two more players Aneef Kelani and Abidah Fatai have been added to the Team Nigeria Eaglets at the Championships. Both players are giving a good account of themselves in the U-15 category.

Fatai Abidah was born in Lagos while Aneef Kelani was born in New York and they’re both students of Heritage Global Academy, Ikorodu, Lagos.

Their voyage into the mind sport has been aided by their very supportive family and one of Africa and Nigeria’s finest Tournament Directors, Khaleel Adedeji, who has been guiding them in the game of scrabble.

The President of the Nigeria Scrabble Federation (NSF), Engineer Olobatoke Aka, had some pleasant words for the Kwara State government for supporting three members of Team Nigeria as well as an accompanying official to the championship.

“We are elated that the Kwara State government is always willing to support scrabble and we are equally happy that the chairman of Lagos State Scrabble and Monopoly Association, Engineer Dipo Akanbi is also backing us.”

The PANASA President’s Cup also started on Thursday in Kenya with about 20 Nigerians participating in the second biggest competition in Africa.

title: Ghanaian Tactician And Sudan Coach, Appiah, Slams Nigeria Weakness After Humiliated The Super Eagles
content:
Ghanaian tactician and Sudan head coach, Kwesi Appiah, after humiliated the home-based Super Eagle of Nigeria with 4-0 victory at the ongoing TotalEnergies CAF African Nations Championship (CHAN) PAMOJA 2024, has berated the team tactical prowess despite acknowledged their quality.

Speaking at the post-match press conference, the Ghanaian tactician revealed that his team had well prepared for a challenging encounter, confident to win but surprise by the score line.

“We knew it would be a tough game, especially in the first 20 minutes. We had to soak up Nigeria’s early pressure and then hit them on the counter. Our performance was much improved compared to the game against Congo,” he said.

“I wasn’t expecting that result. The Nigerian team isn’t bad at all they just need some tactical adjustments.”

The North Africans’ win against Nigeria has now moved them closer to the knockout stages as they face Senegal next, while Nigeria face Congo in their final Group D fixture.

title: CAF Disciplinary Board Imposed Fines On Three African Nations Over Regulation Breaches
content:
The Confédération Africaine de Football (“CAF”) Disciplinary Board after meeting to deliberate on various matters relating to the ongoing TotalEnergies CAF African Nations Championship (“CHAN”) PAMOJA 2024 has found Zambia, Kenya, and Morocco guilty of violating its regulations during the ongoing African Nations Championship (CHAN).

The Board fined Zambia with $5,000 for breaching CAF’s media regulations after failing to present their head coach at the mandatory matchday-one press conference before their clash with the Democratic Republic of Congo.

Kenya received the heaviest penalty — a $50,000 fine — for multiple safety and security lapses during their match against Morocco at the Moi International Sports Centre, Kasarani.

Morocco was sanctioned for the inappropriate conduct of its players during the same fixture against Kenya. CAF imposed a $5,000 fine, with $2,500 suspended on condition that no similar offence is committed for the remainder of the tournament.

The statement read: “The CAF Disciplinary Board charged Football Association of Zambia (“FAZ”) with breaching CAF’s Media Regulations during the Match Day-1 Press Conference ahead of their TotalEnergies CAF African Nations Championship (“CHAN”) match against Democratic Republic of Congo.

Zambia failed to present the head coach at the mandatory Press Conference. The Disciplinary Board found Zambia guilty and imposed a fine of USD 5,000.

“The CAF Disciplinary Board charged the Football Kenya Federation (“FKF”) with multiple safety and security breaches during Kenya TotalEnergies CAF African Nations Championship (“CHAN”) match against Morocco at Moi International Sports Centre, Kasarani.

“The Disciplinary Board found Kenya guilty and imposed a fine of USD 50,000. Kenya was warned that continued failure to meet CAF safety and security requirements may lead to the relocation of Kenya’s National Team matches to an alternative venue. Kenya was advised to increase security measures by deploying sufficient personnel within the perimeter of the stadium as well as adhering to the road closures on match days.

“The CAF Disciplinary Board charged the Fédération Royale Marocaine de Football (“FRMF”) with the inappropriate conduct of its players during Morocco’s TotalEnergies CAF African Nations Championship (“CHAN”) match against Kenya.

“The Disciplinary Board found Morocco guilty and imposed a fine of USD 5,000, of which USD 2,500 is suspended on condition that no similar offence is committed during the remainder of CHAN 2024.

“The fines are to be paid within 60 days of notification of this decision.”

title: Students In Nigeria Tertiary Institutions Set To Face Drug Tests - Education Minister
content:
Followed a meeting in Abuja on Wednesday between the education leaders and Chairman of the National Drug Law Enforcement Agency, Brig Gen Buba Marwa (retd), on the measures to curb substance abuse among Nigeria students, the Minister of Education, Dr Tunji Alausa, has backed the introduction of compulsory and random drug integrity tests for students in tertiary institutions across the country.

The minister also approved a review of the current secondary school curriculum to incorporate updated drug education and committed to forming an inter-ministerial working group with the NDLEA.

According to the NDLEA spokesman, Femi Babafemi, the agency’s had proposed a three-pronged approach: revising drug education content in schools, introducing stand-alone drug abuse prevention programmes in secondary schools, and implementing a drug testing policy for tertiary institutions, including for new students, returning students, and random testing.

“We are fighting for the souls of our children. Without drugs, many criminal activities would not be possible.

“When the youths get into drugs, they won’t go to school, and even when they go to school, they are not getting a functional education.

“At the end of the day, what happens? Their level of critical thinking is lower.

“Their ability to make informed decisions in the later part of their life becomes significantly reduced. So, they become unemployable.

“And what happens? You now have that vicious cycle. They’re not functional. You also said something very important about the drug test policy in tertiary institutions. We will do it. We have to do it. We do not have a choice. At least, we’ll start with tertiary institutions, for their fresh and returning students as well as random testing.

“I would suggest we form a technical working group, an inter-ministerial working group between our ministry and NDLEA. As a result, I would also like to create a Substance Use Prevention Unit in the ministry.

“We’re reviewing the curriculum now for secondary school. And that’s why I’ve asked the Director of Senior Secondary School to come, to be here and then we find a way to cascade it down to primary school.

“We need to incorporate both primary and secondary schools into their curriculum. But the one for secondary school, we can do that now. We’re currently developing their new curriculum.

“Also, on the stand-alone school programmes, I agree with you fully. We should also design ongoing programmes in our schools. That we can roll out, and cascade down,” Alausa stated.

title: 2026 World Cup Qualifier: FIFA Confirms South Africa vs Nigeria Showdown Date
content:
As 2026 FIFA World Cup qualifying getting towards a close, the world football governing body, FIFA, has confirmed date for the crucial qualifying clash between South Africa’s Bafana Bafana and Nigeria’s Super Eagles.

According to FIFA’s Head of Qualifiers and International Matches, Gordon Savic, the Group C encounter will be staged at the 46,000 capacity Toyota Stadium in Bloemfontein, previously known as Vodacom Park and later as Free State Stadium, with kick-off set for 4:00 p.m. GMT (5:00 p.m. Nigeria time, 6:00 p.m. South Africa time) on Tuesday, September 9, 2025.

This fixture is expected to be a decisive encounter in Group C as both nations battle for a spot at the 2026 FIFA World Cup.

title: No Issue With Ooni, Sultan Cannot Be Permanent Co-Chair For Traditional Rulers’ Council - MBF
content:
The Middle Belt Forum (MBF) in a statement signed by MBF National Spokesman, Luka Binniyat, has rejected the proposed bill before the National Assembly to make the Sultan of Sokoto, Alhaji Sa’ad Abubakar the Permanent Co-chairmen of National Council for Traditional Rulers of Nigeria, citing strong historical, cultural, constitutional, as well as moral grounds.

The Forum said the Sokoto Sultanate is historically junior to Middle Belt monarchies. They also distance itself from whatever the Southern region decided on inclusion of the Ooni of Ife as the Permanent Co-chairmen of National Council for Traditional Rulers of Nigeria.

“The Middle Belt Forum (MBF) wishes to categorically express its firm opposition to a contentious clause in the National Council for Traditional Rulers of Nigeria (Establishment) Bill, 2024, currently before the National Assembly.

“The Bill, sponsored by Senator Simon Bako Lalong (Plateau South), who is respected son of the Middle Belt and the Gwad-Goemai of the Goemai ethnic nation, has passed its second reading as of March 2025 and is now under consideration by the Senate Committee on Establishment and Public Service.

“At the heart of the controversy lies a deeply troubling clause in the Bill which proposes that the Sultan of Sokoto and the Ooni of Ife be made permanent co-chairmen of the proposed National Council for Traditional Rulers.

“While we leave our esteemed partners from the Southern region, to determine their position on the inclusion of the Ooni of Ife, the Middle Belt Forum unequivocally rejects, abhors, and condemns the institutionalisation of the Sultan of Sokoto as a permanent co-chairman of this proposed council.

“Historically, the Sokoto Caliphate is a relatively young institution compared to ancient kingdoms and confederacies in the Middle Belt. For instance, the Kwararafa Confederacy, which flourished for centuries, predates the Caliphate.

“Sultan is primarily a religious leader, not a secular traditional monarch. In Nigeria today, the Sultan of Sokoto is widely acknowledged as the spiritual head of all Nigerian Muslims, particularly across the 19 Northern States and the FCT. His spiritual leadership role is fundamentally religious. It is not secular.

“If pass, it would also skew the balance of representation in favour of Islam, thereby promoting religious supremacy under the guise of traditional unity.

“The Middle Belt Forum stands firm in its belief that true national cohesion can only be achieved through fairness, mutual respect, and recognition of our rich historical diversities.

“Any attempt to impose a permanent religious figurehead on a national institution of traditional rulers is a violation of Nigeria’s secular character, cultural heritage, and federal structure. We shall resist it using every lawful and democratic means available to us,” the statement said.

title: Nigeria First Policy: Dangote Presses Tinubu For Ban As Fuel War Brews With The Importers
content:
The President of the Dangote Group, Alhaji Aliko Dangote, speaking during the Global Commodity Insights Conference on West African Refined Fuel Markets hosted by the Nigerian Midstream and Downstream Petroleum Regulatory Authority in partnership with S&P Global Insights, has asked President Bola Tinubu to include refined petroleum products in the list of items banned under the ‘Nigeria First’ policy of the Federal Government.

President Tinubu ’Nigeria First’ policy ban government agencies from importing goods or services that can be produced within Nigeria. Stating that no procurement of foreign goods or services already available in Nigeria shall proceed without justification and a Bureau of Public Procurement waiver.

Dangote request to include petrol, diesel, and other refined petroleum products to the items banned by the policy however got unanimously rejection by oil marketers and some industry analysts on Sunday, citing fight against monopoly.

“The Nigeria First policy announced by His Excellency, President Bola Tinubu, should apply to the petroleum product sector and all other sectors.

“To make matters worse, we are now facing increased dumping of cheap, often toxic petroleum products, some of which are blended to substandard levels that would never be allowed in Europe or North America.

“Due to the price caps on the Russian petroleum products, discounted petroleum products produced in Russia or with discounted Russian crude find their way to Africa, severely undercutting our local production, which is based on full crude pricing. This has created an unlevel playing field in most African countries. Petrol and diesel are sold for about a dollar net of taxes.

“In Nigeria, due to this unfair competition, this price is just about 60 cents, even cheaper than Saudi Arabia, which produces and refines its own oil. This is due to the fact that we are having too much dumping. To remain viable, we urge the governments across Africa to take deliberate steps as the United States, Canada, and the European Union have done to protect domestic producers from unfair competition.

“Let me take this opportunity to address concerns around monopoly and dominance. The reality is that too many people who have the means and the opportunity to contribute meaningfully to our nation’s growth choose instead to criticise from the sidelines while investing their wealth abroad.

“Today, Nigeria has actually become a net exporter of refined products. Before I came on the podium, I asked my people how many tonnes of PMS we have actually exported. From June beginning to date, we have exported about 1 million tonnes of PMS, within the last 50 days,” Dangote said.

However, the marketers, on Sunday, through the National Publicity Secretary of the Independent Petroleum Marketers Association of Nigeria, Chinedu Ukadike, has disagreed with Dangote, urging the Federal Government not to consider adding petroleum products to the list of items banned from importation as it would spell doom for the sector.

“We independent marketers will depart from that request. If the government does that, that means we will not be able to check inflation and monopoly, since it is the only refinery operating in the country now. We should continue to import even as we buy locally.

“I heard that the NMDPRA stated clearly that Dangote cannot produce all the fuel that the country needs. We will appreciate it if the country allows importation to continue since we are not paying subsidy,” Ukadike said.

title: Scientist Warns Nigeria Against Earthquakes, Cites Its Tremor In Some Part Of The Country
content:
Dr Anietie Ikott, the Chief Executive Director of Anirich Nig. Limited, an Akwa Ibom State, Uyo, based scientist has warned that Nigeria may soon experience a devastating earthquake and other climate change-induced disasters, citing the recent tremor in Abuja and some parts of South-West states.

He stated this while speaking in Uyo on Saturday, when disclosing his developed technology that can prevented these disasters.

“We have witnessed frequent climate change-triggered disasters in Nigeria, such as strong winds and the destruction that goes with it, excessive rainfall and flooding that have led to loss of thousands of lives and properties, and destruction of multi-million naira worth of infrastructure, such as happened in Niger and Borno states recently.

“Nigeria will soon experience an earthquake, a very devastating one. We are not immune to earthquakes; they can strike any time, any day.

“Any part of Nigeria that is struck by an earthquake can never be the same again.

“Recently, we have had an earthquake tremor in Abuja, and part of Western State. This is clear proof that we are not immune to earthquakes, he said.

“Earthquakes, excessive rainfall and flooding can be controlled, tornadoes, cyclones, hurricanes, excessive winter ice formation, ice storms, excessive thunderstorms are all controllable and can be controlled with weather control technology,” he added reference to the technology he developed.

title: WAFCON 2024 Awards: Nigeria Duo Named MVP, Best Goalkeeper
content:
Nigeria’s Super Falcons capped their triumphant 2024 Women’s Africa Cup of Nations (WAFCON) campaign with individual accolades to match their collective success, as captain Rasheedat Ajibade was named the tournament’s Most Valuable Player (MVP), and goalkeeper Chiamaka Nnadozie took home the Best Goalkeeper Award.

The 13th edition of the Women’s Africa Cup of Nations not only showcased the growing depth and quality of women’s football across the continent but also reaffirmed Nigeria’s enduring dominance. With 10 titles from 10 finals appearances, the Super Falcons remain the undisputed queens of African football.

Ajibade, the inspirational leader and dynamic winger, was a constant force throughout the competition. Her combination of skill, tenacity, and leadership proved vital as Nigeria stormed to a record-extending 10th WAFCON title. The former Atlético Madrid star was named Woman of the Match in three of Nigeria’s six games and played a decisive role in their thrilling 3–2 victory over host nation Morocco in the final.

At the opposite end of the pitch, Nnadozie provided the bedrock for Nigeria’s success. The newly-signed Brighton shot-stopper was a commanding presence between the posts, conceding just two goals during the entire tournament—both of which came in the high-octane final. Her crucial saves were instrumental in Nigeria’s semi-final triumph over defending champions South Africa, further cementing her reputation as one of Africa’s finest goalkeepers.

Morocco’s Ghizlane Chebbak claimed the Golden Boot, finishing as the tournament’s top scorer with five goals. Her early goal in the final gave the Atlas Lionesses hope, but it ultimately wasn’t enough to prevent Nigeria from staging a stunning comeback.

Meanwhile, South Africa were honoured with the Fair Play Award, in recognition of their exemplary discipline and sportsmanship across the competition.

title: NSC Praise Eniola For Winning Gold Medal at 2025 British and Irish Para-Badminton International
content:
The National Sports Commission (NSC) has congratulated Eniola Bolaji, on her stunning gold medal triumph at the 2025 British and Irish Para-Badminton International, held at the Sport Wales National Centre in Cardiff on Saturday.

Reacting to her victory, Seyi Johnson, Chief of Staff to the Director General of the National Sports Commission, lauded Bolaji’s feat and the leadership of the NSC for its support to para-athletes and other growing sports.

“This gold medal is a reflection of what is possible when talent meets opportunity. We thank the NSC Chairman, Mallam Shehu Dikko, and Director General, Hon. Bukola Olopade, for providing an inclusive and enabling platform where all sports, especially para-sports, can thrive, receive adequate funding, and compete at the highest international level.

“The NSC is charging Bolaji to stay focused and build on this momentum as she prepares for the Commonwealth Games and the Paralympics,” Johnson said.

The victory is particularly significant, as Bolaji had previously lost to Syakuroh in the semifinals of the Paris 2024 Paralympic Games.

However, Bolaji showcased grit and brilliance in the final of the women’s SL3 category, defeating world No. 1 and Tokyo Paralympic silver medalist, Qonitah Ikhtiar Syakuroh of Indonesia, in a thrilling 2-1 match (21-16, 16-21, 21-13) on Court 4.

title: CAF Directive: Super Falcon Players Earn 30% Of N1.5 Billion Prize For The Tenth WAFCON Title
content:
Nigeria’s Super Falcons, after clinching their record-extending 10th Women’s Africa Cup of Nations (WAFCON) against Morocco on Saturday night, said to entitle to billions of Naira.

The final which took place at Prince Moulay Abdellah Stadium in Rabat, saw the Falcons in a dramatic comeback to overcome a two-goal deficit in a pulsating final that will go down as one of the most memorable in the tournament’s history. The victory capped off Nigeria’s “Mission X” campaign, a symbolic reference to their pursuit of a 10th continental crown.

The host has a first half lead with the opening goal from Ghizlane Chebbak in the 8th minute, before doubled it via Sanaâ Mssoudy in 24 minute, taking a commanding 2-0 lead into the break.

However, Nigeria responded with grit and class in the second half. Tactical adjustments from head coach Justin Madugu, including the introduction of Rinsola Babajide and Jennifer Echegini, turned the tide in Nigeria’s favour.

Esther Okoronkwo open the score line for the Falcon in the 64 minutes from the penalty spot after a Moroccan handball in the area, before Forward Opeyemi Ijamilusi  equalized in the 71 minute to level with the Moroccans. The third goals that zeal the victory came in the 88 minute through Echegini who delivered the final blow, slotting home the winner to silence the home crowd and etch her name into Super Falcons folklore.

For their triumph, the Super Falcons were rewarded with $1 million (over ₦1.5 billion), as the Confederation of African Football (CAF) announced a 100% increase in prize money for the tournament winner. The total prize pool for the 2024 edition of WAFCON was also raised by 45%, reflecting CAF’s growing investment in women’s football across the continent.

Meanwhile, CAF instructed that the Nigeria Football Federation give 30 percent of the money to the players.

CAF WAFCON 2024 Prize Money Breakdown:

Winner: $1,000,000

Runner-Up: $500,000

Third Place: $350,000

Fourth Place: $300,000

Quarter-Finalists (4 Teams): $200,000 each

Third in Group: $150,000

Fourth in Group (3 Teams): $125,000 each.

title: Nigeria's 10th WAFCON Title Under Threat As Morocco Awaits CAF Verdict Over Eligibility
content:
The Super Falcons' historic 10th Women's Africa Cup of Nations (WAFCON) title risking stripped off as the Confederation of African Football (CAF) opens an investigation into a complaints filed by the Moroccan Football Federation (MFF)

MFF just some hours before the 2025 WAFCON final in Rabat had filed a petition to challenge the eligibility of Nigerian defenders Ashleigh Plumptre and Michelle Alozie, citing alleged inconsistencies in their nationality documentation. The situation many considered as the last-minute ploy to destabilize Nigeria’s preparations.

Despite the looming off-field controversy before the game, Nigeria went ahead to defeats the host nation Morocco 3–2 in a thrilling contest to claim a record-extending tenth continental crown.

Should CAF uphold Morocco’s protest, Nigeria might be stripped of the title. However, if the case is dismissed, the Super Falcons are set to receive a $1 million (approximately ₦1.5 billion) prize as WAFCON champions.

title: Mariam, Aruna Quadri Daughter, Set For Nigeria Debut At Africa Youth Championships
content:
The daughter of Nigerian table tennis icon Quadri Aruna, Mariam Aruna, is poised to make her debut for the country at the ITTF Africa Youth Championships, scheduled for Sunday, July 27 to Sunday, August 3 at the Molade Okoya-Thomas Hall, Teslim Balogun Stadium, Lagos.

The 12-year-old is part of Nigeria’s U-15 girls’ team alongside Fatimoh Ahmed, Chinenye Okafor, and Aziza Sezuo that will compete against players from 10 other nations, including Egypt, Tunisia, Uganda, and South Africa.

Earlier this year, she and her siblings secured podium finishes at the João Monteiro Table Tennis Tournament in Portugal.

title: Nigerians On Certificate Of Sponsorship Visa Risk Deportation With The New UK Rules
content:
The recent development from British government by removing over 100 jobs including skilled worker roles from CoS eligibility, while the salary thresholds for other jobs on the scheme also increased by at least 30 per cent in an efforts to control immigration has cause panic among Nigerians working in the United Kingdom on Certificate of Sponsorship or Skilled Worker visas.

The new regulations, which took effect on July 22, 2025, affect various visa routes, including the Skilled Worker, Health and Care visas, along with the requirements for sponsoring foreign workers. It also increased the general Skilled Worker salary threshold to £41,700 or higher depending on the role, while removed lower-skilled roles (previously at RQF Level 3–5) from CoS eligibility unless they appear on a newly created Temporary Shortage Occupation List.

Some of the delisted jobs include managers and proprietors in agriculture, forestry, hospitality, and logistics (SOC 1211–1258); health, community and welfare roles such as dispensing opticians, pharmaceutical technicians, youth and community workers, and counsellors (SOC 3211–3224); protective service roles like police officers (sergeant and below), fire service officers, and prison officers (SOC 3312–3314); as well as creative and performing arts professionals, including artists, authors, translators, actors, dancers, photographers, and interior or fashion designers (SOC 3411–3429), among others.

Though, no Nigerians have been sacked because of the new regulations, but their fate will hang in the balance because at the end of their current sponsorship, those whose jobs have been removed from CoS eligibility will not be able to find a new job in that category, and their visa will not be renewed.

Again, the challenges those whose jobs were retained under the new regulations will face is that their employers may not be able to pay the new salary threshold, which has risen to £41,700 from £24,000, £25,000 or £26,000 per annum.

The sponsorship is usually between one and five years, by the time that it expires will companies be able to pay the new salary threshold? And those whose jobs has been removed will they be able to find new job that meet the requirements? Hence, they become an illegal immigrant if unable.

title: WAFCON Final: Lifts The Trophy In Rabat – Madugu, Oparanozie, Charge Falcons
content:
Nigeria’s Super Falcons Coach. Justine Madugu has said the Falcons did not come this far at the 13th Women Africa Cup of Nations to think of anything but reclaiming the trophy they have won a total of nine times out of the previous 12 championships, urging the team to gunning for trophy and make it 10th.

“We thank God for making it to the final. I want to assure you that we are not going to relent or take our eyes off the ball. Our focus is on lifting the trophy in Rabat on Saturday.

“We knew South Africa as Cup holders would be difficult but we were ready for them, and I am glad that our tactics paid off. As I said before the tournament, we will always assess the opposition first and then determine what tactics would suit us better and serve our purpose. We have done these in our previous five games and we will do the same in the final,” he said.

So also the former Super Falcons striker, Desire Oparanozie,  who urged her colleague to finish their mission by clinching a record-extending 10th Women’s Africa Cup of Nations (WAFCON) title after their impressive 2-1 semi-final victory over defending champions South Africa on Tuesday.

"Yes, I think they can win WAFCON. Nigeria has talented players with winning experience, and I’m confident they will get the required result.

"They have all been great. Every one of them has shown up as a team, a really effective team; they’ve all been very brilliant on the field.

"This WAFCON edition has been thrilling, with top teams and players showcasing their skills and making history in every game. It’s a testament to how much women’s football in Africa has grown.

"Winning games is no longer a walk in the park every win comes from hard work. Teams are pushing themselves to earn their victories, and that’s very impressive," Oparanozie told Showmax Premier League.

title: WAFCON 2024: CAF Appoints East Africa Officials For Nigeria vs Morocco Final
content:
As the curtain drawn to a close, the Confederation of African Football (CAF) has appointed Namibia’s Antsino to officiate the final of the 2024 Women’s Africa Cup of Nations (WAFCON) between Nigeria and Morocco.

She’s one of the most consistent and composed referees in the tournament. Antsino will be the first Namibian official to take charge of a WAFCON final, and will be assisted by Alice Umutesi of Rwanda (Assistant Referee 1) and Senegal’s Tabara Mbodji (Assistant Referee 2), both praised for their sharp judgment and steady performances during the competition.

In the Video Assistant Referee (VAR) booth, Rwanda’s Salima Mukansanga a trailblazer in global football officiating will take charge, bringing her wealth of experience to the high-stakes encounter.

title: National Sports Commission Submits Official Bid To Host Formula 1 Grand Prix In Abuja
content:
The Chairman of the National Sports Commission, Mallam Shehu Dikko, in a statement released on Wednesday has announced that the commission have officially entered the race to host a Formula 1 Grand Prix in Abuja to positioning itself in becoming the first African nation in more than three decades to stage the prestigious motorsport event

“We are exploring all possibilities to bring Formula 1 to Nigeria as soon as practicable not just as a sporting event, but as a catalytic driver of tourism, infrastructure development, youth engagement, and economic growth.

“Hosting the F1 race would not only boost national pride and attract worldwide attention but also create thousands of jobs and significantly strengthen local infrastructure,” Dikko said.

title: Remo Stars Dominate Super Eagle Coach, Chelle, 2025 CHAN Selection
content:
Head Coach Eric Chelle has announced the list of 23 players that make up the final squad of Super Eagles B for the 8th African Nations Championship taking place in Kenya, Tanzania and Uganda, 2nd – 30th August.

The selected team has Junior Harrison Nduka as captain, and well dominated by Remo Stars players.

The team has been training for several weeks at the Remo Stars Sports Institute in Ikenne-Remo, Ogun State, and expected to travel out of the country to Zanzibar on Thursday evening, aboard an Ethiopian Airline aircraft.

Nigeria are in group D alongside Cup holders Senegal, Sudan and Congo.

The Super Eagles will play their first two matches of the competition, against Senegal and Sudan, at the Amman Stadium on the island of Zanzibar, before taking on Congo at the Benjamin Mkapa Stadium in Dar es Salaam.

title: Youth Games: Nigeria Weightlifting Federation Begins Implementation of New Bodyweights Categories
content:
The Nigeria Weightlifting Federation (NWF) will begin implementation of the new bodyweight categories at the 9th National Youth Games (NYG) in Asaba, Delta State.

The Youth Games which will commence from 29th August through 6th September will feature over 30 sporting events including Weightlifting.

The Nigeria Weightlifting Federation (NWF) on Monday informed all coaches, stakeholders and officials that it would implement the new bodyweights as approved by the International Weightlifting Federation (IWF).

The Federation in a press release signed by the Media Officer, Amaechi Agbo, directed all coaches and State Associations to ensure that their athelets enlisted for the NYG complies to the new bodyweight categories.

A total of six bodyweight categories comprising three each for men and women will feature in the weightlifting event at the NYG Asaba 2025.

The new bodyweight categories for men are: 56kg, 60kg and 65kg.

The new bodyweight categories for women are: 44kg, 48kg and 53kg.

It could be recalled that the International Weightlifting Federation (IWF) began implementing the new bodyweight categories for senior, junior, and youth athletes from June 1, 2025 as ratified by the Executive Board

These changes include eight classifications for both men and women in senior and junior divisions, and for youth, there are eight categories for both boys and girls.

A breakdown of the new categories include

Senior & Junior:

Men: 60kg, 65kg, 71kg, 79kg, 88kg, 98kg, 110kg, +110kg

Women: 48kg, 53kg, 58kg, 63kg, 69kg, 77kg, 86kg, +86kg

Youth:

Men: 56kg, 60kg, 65kg, 71kg, 79kg, 88kg, 98kg, +98kg

Women: 44kg, 48kg, 53kg, 58kg, 63kg, 69kg, 77kg, +77kg

36 States of the Federation as well as the Federal Capital Territory are expected to participate in the weightlifting event at the National Youth Games in Asaba, Delta State.

title: WAFCON 2025: Super Falcons Booked Final Ticket For The 10th Time After Win Over South Africa
content:
Nigeria, after a dramatic semi-final win over South Africa in Casablanca on Tuesday has reached the Final of the 13th Women Africa Cup of Nations, thanks to a late-in-the-day spectacular goal by defender Michelle Alozie.

The nine times winner, Super Falcon will now battle the host nation Morocco in the final match after the later defeated Ghana 4:2 in a penalty shootout.

Rasheedat Ajibade gave Nigeria the lead in the 45th minute, calmly converting a penalty to make it 1-0 heading into the break. However, South Africa responded strongly in the second half, leveling the score in the 60th minute through Linda Motlhalo's penalty kick, before Michelle Alozie scored the winning goal deep into stoppage time in the 90+4th minute after a setup from Esther Okoronkwo.

The thrilling 2-1 victory over South Africa’s Banyana Banyana in the semi-finals meant the Super Falcons’ first win over the Banyana in the Woman Africa Cup of Nations in three times both have meet in the tournaments, with the South Africans having won group stages matches in 2018 and 2022 with 1-0 and 2-1 score-lines respectively.

title: #Missionx: NSC Lauded Super Falcons For Picking WAFCON Final Ticket After Semi-Final Victory Over SA
content:
The National Sports Commission (NSC) has applauds the resilience and fighting spirit of the Super Falcons of Nigeria following their 2-1 semi-final victory over South Africa on Tuesday, in the Women’s Africa Cup of Nations (WAFCON) to booked their place in the tournament’s final.

The nine time champions took the lead in the first half through Captain Rasheedat Ajibade from a penalty kick before South Africa’s Linda Motlhalo equalized, also from penalty spot. But in dramatic fashion, Michelle Alozie sealed the victory with a stunning last-minute goal, sending the Super Falcons into the WAFCON final.

Reacting to the win, NSC Chairman, Mallam Shehu Dikko, praised the Super Falcons for their tenacity and urged them to remain focused on the ultimate prize.

“This victory was a display of who we are as Nigerians. The Super Falcons showed grit, class, and composure under pressure. But the mission is not yet accomplished. Our eyes must remain on the trophy. We want to make history by lifting the WAFCON title for a record 10th time,” Dikko said.

On his part, the Director General of the NSC, Hon. Bukola Olopade, congratulate Super Falcons for the victory and also extend gratitude to the Nigeria Football Federation (NFF) led by Alhaji Ibrahim Gusau, for their leadership and the team’s excellent preparation ahead of the tournament.

“The NSC commends the NFF board for putting the team in excellent shape. The team has put in a lot of hardwork and it’s obvious to see, from the results. However, this is not the time to over celebrate. Let’s stay locked in on the final. Naija no de carry last and so fight to be crowned African champions for the tenth time,” Olopade stated.

title: African Champions, Nigeria’s D’tigress Pay Courtesy Visit To National Sports Commission Leadership
content:
Ahead of their title defense at the 29th FIBA Women’s Afrobasket Championship, Reigning African champions, Nigeria’s women’s basketball team, “D’Tigress” paid a courtesy visit to the leadership of the National Sports Commission (NSC).

The team was hosted in Abuja on Tuesday by the NSC Chairman, Mallam Shehu Dikko, and the Director General, Hon. Bukola Olopade. D’Tigress, who have emerged victorious in the last four editions of the continental showpiece, were warmly received and celebrated by the Commission for their consistency and excellence on the African stage.

Chairman of the NSC, Mallam Shehu Dikko stated thus: “D’Tigress have made Nigeria proud on numerous occasions, and we remain firmly behind them. Winning four straight Afrobasket titles is no small feat, and the entire nation is rooting for you to make it five. You are not just champions, you are role models to a lot of young girls in Africa.”

Dikko went ahead to ask the team to table their immediate needs as they get set to jet out for their title defence. The Commission wasted no time in approving the requests presented by the players, underscoring the Commission’s commitment to athlete welfare.

Hon. Bukola Olopade lauded the team for being a beacon of hope and inspiration, assuring them of the nation’s full support, as they gear up to defend their crown in Abidjan, Côte d’Ivoire, from July 25th to August 3rd.

Also present at the event were key stakeholders in the Nigerian sports ecosystem, including the Senior Special Assistant to the President on Grassroots Sports, Adeboye Adeyinka Anthony; Director General of the National Institute of Sports, Rt. Hon. Phillip Shuaibu; President of the Nigeria Olympic Committee (NOC), Habu Gumel; head of Elite Athlete Development and Podium Board, Yusuf Alli; and the 2nd Vice President of the Athletics Federation of Nigeria (AFN), Miss Aku Aghazu.

The 29th edition of the Women’s Afrobasket will feature 12 countries battling for continental glory. Nigeria heads into the tournament as the defending champions, having defeated Senegal 84–74 in the 2023 final in Kigali, Rwanda.

The D’Tigress also triumphed over Senegal in 2017 and 2019, and beat Mali in the 2021 final, asserting dominance on the continent over the past decade.

title: Relief As Enugu Electricity Crashes Band A Tariff To N160/Kwh
content:
The Enugu State Electricity Regulatory Commission (EERC) has directed the MainPower Electricity Distribution Limited, the utility company that succeeded Enugu Electricity Distribution Company to review down electricity cost for Band A customers from N209 per kilowatt-hour to N160/kWh, effective August 1, 2025.

The order was contained in the Enugu commission’s Order No. EERC/2025/003 entitled ‘Tariff Order for MainPower Electricity Distribution Limited 2025’ issued on Sunday, stating that the decision was based on cost reflective, insisting tariff must reflect the power generation subsidy by the Federal Government for the benefit of electricity consumers.

The Enugu State Electricity Law 2023 signed by Governor Peter Mbah in September 2023, in pursuant to the 2023 Constitutional Amendment, which firmly established the legislative authority of the states on electricity matters within their states empowers EERC to control its electricity market, regulate the activities of operators in power generation, transmission, and distribution in and exclusively for the state.

“We reviewed their entire costs, using our Tariff Methodology Regulations 2024, and the supporting Distribution Tariff Model to get an average price of N94. The price is low because the Federal Government has been subsidising electricity generation cost, which charges only N45 out of the actual cost of N112. That was how we came about the average tariff of N94 as a cost-reflective tariff at our level as a subnational electricity market.

“Breaking this across the various tariff bands means that Band A will be paying N160 while other Bands B, C, D, and E are frozen. Band A, at N160, will help MainPower to manage the rate shock, and if the subsidy is removed, the savings will assist them in stabilising the tariff over a defined period of time. Nevertheless, at all times, the tariff will be cost-reflective and will not require any state subsidy.

“However, the N160 Band A tariff could be difficult to sustain should the Federal Government remove the generation tariff subsidy currently being enjoyed by electricity consumers throughout the country, as tariffs would likely rise beyond these new rates.

“But until then, it is only right that Ndi Enugu – Band A customers enjoy the reduced tariff effective August 1, 2025,” EERC Chairman, Chijioke Okonkwo stated.

title: NMA: Doctors To Commence Nationwide Strike By Thursday
content:
Nigerian Medical Association, through its President, Prof Bala Audu, during an interview with Punch has warned that the association will ground medical services nationwide if the federal government fails to meet its demands as the ultimatum period end by Wednesday, July 23.

Recalls, NMA had on July 2, issued a 21-day ultimatum in protest against a circular from the National Salaries, Incomes and Wages Commission on revised allowances for medical and dental officers in the federal public service, which the doctors kicked against for violating prior agreements.

“We have made our position clear. The ultimatum ends on July 23, and if the Federal Government does not address our demands, we may have no choice but to proceed with a strike.

“We have rejected that circular outright. We expect that any new directive affecting our members should be the outcome of mutual consultation, not something imposed.

“The last meeting happened two weeks ago and the Coordinating Minister of Health and Social Welfare, Prof Muhammad Pate; the Minister of State for Health and Social Welfare, Dr Iziaq Salako; the Permanent Secretary, the Director of Hospital Services, and the representative of minister of labour were at the meeting, and some affiliate of the NMA were present, and I was part of that meeting as well.

“The minister appreciated us, then he spoke about the issues as contained in the list of demands from the NMA.

“However, he felt that we should go for a further meeting, and another meeting was slated for last week, unfortunately, in the week, we lost the former President Muhammadu Buhari, so the meeting couldn’t be held.

“However, the next meeting is supposed to happen between us, the National Salaries, Incomes and Wages Commission, which issued a circular that we feel is obnoxious, and we have rejected it. We would also meet with the Ministry of Finance and representatives from the Ministry of Health.

“We expect that after the funeral ceremonies, government stakeholders will reconvene with us, hopefully by Monday. Otherwise, the 21-day ultimatum still stands. And if the government fails to prioritise this matter, a strike may be inevitable,” he said.

title: NASS VS Natasha: Senate Prepared For Battle Over Natasha’s Forceful Return
content:
Following a media reports quoting the embattled lawmaker representing Kogi Central Senatorial District, Natasha Akpoti-Uduaghan, stating that she would return to the Senate on Tuesday based on a judgment delivered by Justice Binta Nyako of the Federal High Court in Abuja. The Senate has warned the suspended lawmaker to desist from forceful return to the Senate chambers, insisting that no valid court order mandated her immediate recall.

In a statement released on Sunday by the Senate Committee Chairman on Media and Public Affairs, Yemi Adaramodu, the senate warn Senator Natasha against any forcefully resumption. Saying that the Senate had previously issued two public statements after the court ruling and the release of the Certified True Copy of the enrolled order, making it clear that no positive or mandatory directive was issued against the Senate regarding her recall.

“The Senate of the Federal Republic of Nigeria wishes to reaffirm, for the third time, that there is no subsisting court order mandating the Senate to recall Senator Natasha Akpoti-Uduaghan before the expiration of her suspension.

“Rather, the honourable court gave a non-binding advisory urging the Senate to consider amending its standing orders and reviewing the suspension, which it opined might be excessive.

“The court, however, explicitly held that the Senate did not breach any law or constitutional provision in imposing the disciplinary measure based on the senator’s misconduct during plenary, but found her guilty of contempt and imposed penalties, including a N5m fine payable to the Federal Government and a mandatory apology in two national newspapers and on her Facebook page — a directive that has reportedly not been complied with.

“It is, therefore, surprising and legally untenable that Senator Akpoti-Uduaghan, while on appeal and having filed a motion for stay against the valid and binding orders made against her, is attempting to act upon an imaginary order of recall that does not exist.

“The Senate will, at the appropriate time, consider the advisory opinion of the court on both amending the standing orders of the Senate, her recall, and communicate the same thereof to Senator Akpoti-Uduaghan.

“Until then, she is respectfully advised to stay away from the Senate chambers and allow due process to run its full course,” the statement read.

title: Chelle Outline Criteria For Super Eagles Call-Ups
content:
Super Eagles head coach, Eric Chelle, has roll out the criteria he considers before inviting players to the Nigerian national team during a conversation with Onze Mondial.

The France-born tactician has stayed true to his word by consistently selecting players who are physically fit, active and regular at their respective clubs.

“First of all, you need to have playing time. You must be in top physical shape and, of course, you have to be good.

“Physically, a player must be fit. But beyond that, he needs to be tactically intelligent to understand and execute my instructions.

“You also need good technical quality. And finally, you must be mentally ready,” Chelle said.

title: Usyk Knockout Dubois In Fifth-Round To Reclaim Undisputed Heavyweight Crown
content:
The Ukrainian, Oleksandr Usyk, has reaffirmed his status as boxing’s undisputed heavyweight world champion on Saturday night with a devastating fifth-round knockout of Britain’s Daniel Dubois in front of a roaring crowd at Wembley Stadium.

Usyk floored Dubois with a thunderous overhand right, then followed up with a crushing left hook to seal the win and reclaim the IBF belt he had vacated last year.

The victory settles the score after a controversial first bout in 2023, where Dubois was ruled to have landed a low blow that gave Usyk time to recover before securing a ninth-round stoppage. This time, there was no controversy—only brilliance.

“It’s enough. Next? I don’t know. I want to rest. My family, my wife, my children—I want to rest now. Two or three months, I want to just rest. But 38 is a young guy, remember! It’s only the start!

“I want to say thank you to Jesus Christ. I want to say thank you to my team and Wembley—thank you so much! This is for the people,” he said.

title: 2024 WAFCON: Morocco Face Ghana, As Nigeria Eyes Revenge Against South Africa In Semifinal
content:
The final four of the CAF TotalEnergies Women’s Africa Cup of Nations Morocco 2024 showcases the continent’s finest, a host nation propelled by a rare wave of home support, a Ghanaian side on a mission, the reigning champions still standing, and the historical giant with an unmatched pedigree.

On Tuesday, two high-stakes semifinals take center stage, Morocco vs Ghana at the Olympic Stadium in Rabat and South Africa vs Nigeria in the cauldron of Stade Larbi Zaouli in Casablanca.

Morocco vs Ghana: Ambition Meets Determination

Three years ago, Morocco reached the final on home soil, reigniting national pride in women’s football. In 2025, the Atlas Lionesses have matured, stronger and more composed. With a packed Olympic Stadium behind them, Jorge Vilda’s side has shown new-found maturity. Their 3-1 quarterfinal win over Mali, powered by an Ibtissam Jraïdi brace, reinforced their momentum. “This team knows how to endure and strike at the right time. There’s chemistry, there’s soul,” said Vilda post-match.

However, a different challenge awaits. Ghana has maintained relentless intensity throughout the tournament. The Black Queens, led by goalkeeper Cynthia Konlan, hero of their penalty shootout win against Algeria (0-0, 4-2 on penalties)—are a team on a mission. Head coach Kim Björkegren has been clear: “This team has been underestimated for too long. We want to shake things up.”

In the group stage, Ghana emerged from a tough pool with South Africa, Mali, and Tanzania, conceding just two goals and Tanzania, conceding just two goals and finishing with four points. They’ve since ridden a wave of self-belief, exemplified by playmaker Alice Kusi and the energetic Chantelle Boye—a mix of experience and fierce ambition.

Statistically, Morocco boasts one of the tournament’s best attacks (10 goals in four matches), while Ghana holds the best defensive record (only two goals conceded). The matchup is finely balanced. Home advantage might tilt the scales, but Ghana remains unfazed. “Playing the host nation is exciting, not pressure,” Kusi smiled.

South Africa vs Nigeria: A Final Before the Final

This is a classic rivalry, one etched into the very fabric of the CAF TotalEnergies Women’s AFCON. Nigeria has impressed with its discipline: two group wins and one draw, four goals scored, none conceded, and a commanding 5-0 quarterfinal demolition of Zambia. Within a cohesive squad, full-back Michelle Alozie and midfielder Rasheedat Ajibade have stood out, while Esther Okoronkwo, the tournament’s top assist provider with three, continues to rise.

On the other side, Desiree Ellis has instilled her methodical approach. South Africa faced hurdles but endured. After a 1-1 group draw with Tanzania, they edged Senegal on penalties (0-0, 4-1) in the quarterfinals, thanks to the brilliance of goalkeeper Andile Dlamini.

Still, there’s more to this team than meets the eye. Jermaine Seoposenwe, Hildah Magaia, and Lebogang Ramalepe are all capable of turning the game on its head. The possession-heavy style that once seemed toothless now looks sharper, and the squad seems to be reliving the spirit of their 2022 triumph. “There’s a fire, a collective memory. We know what this match means. We know what it takes to beat Nigeria,” Ellis insisted.

By the numbers, Nigeria dominates most categories: best attack (nine goals), best defense (no goals conceded). However, their most recent meeting in the CAF Women’s AFCON ended in a 2-1 victory for South Africa.

The final four of this 2024 Women’s Africa Cup of Nations encapsulates everything promising about African women’s football. Morocco dreams of its first title. Ghana seeks a return to glory. South Africa eyes back-to-back crowns. Nigeria is out to remind everyone who’s boss.

Credit - CAF

title: My Sabbatical Leave From Music - Mr Eazi Opens Up
content:
Nigerian musician, Oluwatosin Ajibade, popularly known as Mr Eazi, in a post shared on X has finally opened up about his year-long break from the music industry, stating that it was intentional to take a step back to rest and recharge after years of nonstop work.

“I’ve been on holiday all year. I started feeling guilty but then I realised I’ve been working since I was 15!! Rest is a blessing! Choplife season!,” he wrote.

Mr Eazi’s took break from music after the release of his long-anticipated debut solo album, The Evil Genius, in 2023.The album which received critical acclaim for its originality, pushing the boundaries of what a modern African album could look and feel like.

title: Mercy Johnson Fired At Ghanaian Television Station For Unauthorised Broadcast
content:
Following broadcasting one of her movie “The Firstborn” without her consent, the Popular Nollywood actress, Mercy Johnson, on her Instagram account has called out the Ghanaian television station, Blazing TV for unauthorised airing.

Sharing the screenshot of a fan’s message alerting her to the unauthorised airing, she express shock and frustration, questioning how such a broadcast could happen without proper licensing.

“Ghana, Blazing TV… How is this even ok? Blazing TV in Ghana is airing my movie, ‘The Firstborn,’ without my consent. How does this even make sense? I am speechless at the audacity of it all,” she wrote.

Recall that earlier this year, Actress Bimbo Ademoye, called out several Ghanaian TV stations for unauthorised airings of her films, tagging top officials including Ghana’s Minister of Communications and the CEO of the National Film Authority to take action. So also filmmaker Omoni Oboli, who criticised Ghanaian broadcasters in April for consistently airing Nigerian content without permission, described it shameful.

title: 2027 Election: ADC Party Constitution Phase-out Obi, Backs Others
content:
The former presidential candidate of Labour Party in the 2023 general election, Peter Obi, has been ruled out from contesting African Democratic Congress (ADC) party ticket for 2027 general election due to the party’s constitution which disqualified individuals affiliated with other political parties from seeking the party’s top ticket.

Obi, who has openly identified with the ADC and declared his intention to contest the presidency in 2027, is yet to resign his membership of the Labour Party as do others in likes of former vice president Atiku Abubakar and ex-Rivers governor Rotimi Amaechi  from PDP and APC respectively.

According to the ADC’s third schedule – guidelines for the conduct of primaries has it’s contained in Article 8 on membership, stipulates that only registered, card-carrying members of the party who are not affiliated with any other political party are eligible to seek nomination for public office.

Article 8 stipulates that a person “must not belong to any other political party and if previously affiliated, must have resigned from such membership.”

This clause appears to pose a significant hurdle to Obi, who has not formally declared any switch to the ADC from LP, allowing the likes of Atiku and Amaechi getting the party’s ticket becoming brighter.

title: Anambra Governorship Candidate For The Upcoming 2025 State Election Shot In Abuja
content:
Chief Jude Ezenwafor, the governorship candidate of Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) for the upcoming 2025 Anambra State election, has been shot by unknown gunmen on Friday night around the Wuse 2 in Abuja while returning home from an appointment.

Ezenwafor was a former presidential aspirant under the Labour Party before returning to the PDP where he picked the party’s ticket as its flagbearer for the Anambra State governorship election scheduled later this year.

His media team confirmed that he sustained multiple gunshot wounds and was immediately rushed to the emergency unit of an undisclosed hospital.

Speaking to journalists from the hospital where he’s currently receiving treatment described the incident as a near-death experience.

“I’m currently in the hospital. The doctors are making efforts to operate me so that they can pull out bullets from my body,” Ezenwafor said.

Security agencies were yet to issue an official statement, but a source close to the PDP campaign team said the matter has been reported to the police and an investigation was underway.

title: CPC Bloc May Get Villa Nod For APC Chairman
content:
Indications from the Presidential Villa shows that the slot for All Progressive Progress (APC) Chairman might be given to the Congress for Progressives Congress (CPC) bloc which was under the control of late former president Muhammadu Buhari.

CPC was one of the political parties that merged to form the All Progressive Progress (APC) in February 2013 ahead of the 2015 general election which later defeated the incumbent government.

So far, former Nasarawa State governor, Tanko Almakura; former Plateau State, Joshua Dariye and Prof Kailani have been consulting and lobbying party leaders for support ahead of the July 25 National Executive Committee (NEC) meeting which is projected to produce a new chairman of the party, after Dr Abdullahi Ganduje recently resigned.

Although the NEC would decide who the party chairman becomes, President Bola Tinubu’s position will be pivotal to the position taken by the party organ.

LEADERSHIP reports that a party source did said that Villa had not taken a final position on the matter but seems tilted towards giving it to the CPC bloc. “The reality is that deliberations are still ongoing. There have been various proposals on the table. Some governors are pushing for a Christian minister from the North Central to get the position.

“But that is being countered by those who think doing that will alienate the Muslim voters there who argue that the zone already enjoys a major Christian appointment there.

“There are also those who are proposing that the current acting chairman should be allowed to continue and conduct a national convention that would usher in a new party leadership.

“But over all, there is a strong sense that the villa is leaning towards the CPC bloc of the party to ensure their integration in the party and starve off the antics of their former members who have joined the ADC coalition.”

The former minister of communication, Adebayo Shittu, who is from the CPC camp also said as much as there was an APC chairmanship contest from the CPC bloc, they were more interested in a committed APC chairman.

“I know of a CPC person who is contesting for national chairman and I know he is committed to APC. I am in APC I am not leaving the party or involved in any counter activity. We are working hard and I am sure that the person who is contesting is very committed to the APC.

“On the issue of what happens next if he does succeed, I can say nothing will happen. What matters is that an APC person becomes national chairman. We don’t want to be the chairman of the party because we are CPC. That is not the issue. We are in the party as members. As far as we are concerned there is nothing like CPC.

“CPC has since been dissolved. As far as we are concerned it is only opportunists that will say as long as they don’t have something they will have to exit APC. But there is nothing like that as far as we are concerned,” he said.

title: WAFCON 2024: Super Falcons Silence Copper Queens To Book Semi-Final Berth
content:
The Super Falcons of Nigeria has defeated Copper Queens of Zambian 5-0 in the quarter final of the 2024 Women’s Africa Cup of Nations (WAFCON) ongoing in Morocco on Friday to book their semi-final.

The Nigeria national team lead with three goals in the first half before added brace in the second half to make it 5:0 past the Zambian team.

Osinachi Ohale open the scoring with header from Esther Okoronkwo’s free kick in the second minute of play at the Stade Larbi Zaouli, Casablanca, before Okoronkwo doubled the lead in the 33rd minute, while

Chinwendu Ihezuo made it 3-0 in the 45th minute to complete a dominant first half display.

In the 68th minute, Tosin Demehin scored her first ever goal for Nigeria with a header, before Folashade Ijamilusi round it up as she converted the fifth goal from low pass from Ajibade in the additional minutes of the second half.

The team has scored eight goals without conceding in the four games played.

Up next is a semi final clash with either holders South Africa or Senegal in the semi final on Tuesday.

title: President Tinubu has approved the South-East investment initiative
content:
In an effort to boost industrial growth in the southeast region of Nigeria, president Tinubu has given his executive approval for the creation of the South-East Investment Company (SEIC). This specialized investment entity will function under the South East Development Commission (SEDC) with the aim of harnessing private capital, boosting regional competitiveness, and accelerating industrial development in the South-East region.

The President's choice comes after receiving the SEDC's report detailing their performance over the past 100 days, along with an official request to establish a subsidiary dedicated solely to securing long-term funding and spearheading transformative economic initiatives in the area.

The SEIC is designed to function as an independently governed investment entity, driven by private-sector leadership, and not reliant on yearly government budgets. Its strategic approach is inspired by the legacy of the Eastern Nigeria Development Corporation (ENDC), which, during Dr. Michael Okpara's leadership, led industrial transformation in the former Eastern Region.

The establishment of SEIC signifies a renewed focus on long-term economic planning that leverages regional strengths, fosters innovation, and encourages collaboration with the private sector.

During a brief ceremony held at the State House, President Tinubu handed over the Certificate of Incorporation for the SEIC to the South East Development Commission. The event was attended by the Honourable Minister of Regional Development, Engr. Abubakar Momoh, the Managing Director/CEO of the SEDC, Mr. Mark Okoye, and members of the Commission's Executive Management Team.

title: Former Ekiti Governor, Fayose, Weeps Over N6.9bn Fraud Court Verdict
content:
Former Ekiti State Governor, Ayodele Fayose, broke down outside the courtroom on Wednesday as the Federal High Court sitting in Lagos discharged him of N6.9bn fraud case filed by the Economic and Financial Crimes Commission.

The Economic and Financial Crimes Commission had accused Fayose and his company, Spotless Investment Limited, of laundering N6.9bn during his tenure as governor between 2014 and 2018. They alleged that Fayose took N1.2bn to fund his 2014 election campaign and received $5m in cash from a sitting minister of state for defence at the time, Musiliu Obanikoro, without using financial institutions.

He was also accused of laundering over N1.6bn through proxies and companies like De Privateer Ltd and Still Earth Ltd, in violation of the Money Laundering (Prohibition) Act, 2011.

At the last hearing of the almost seven-year trial on May 19, 2025, Fayose’s lead counsel, Chief Kanu Agabi (SAN), urged the court to dismiss the charges, argued that the prosecution presented no credible evidence linking Fayose to any criminal act.

In response, counsel for the EFCC, Mr Rotimi Jacobs (SAN), urged the court to reject the submissions, citing a counter-affidavit and written address dated May 8, 2025, argued that Fayose’s failure to use his accounts for the transactions was suspicious and required explanation.

Delivering the judgement, Justice Aneke ruled that the EFCC failed to prove a prima facie case, and consequently discharged and acquitted both defendants.

However, EFCC announced plans to appeal the judgment.

title: No Justification For Nigeria Generating Lower Than 60,000MW Of Electricity – Dangote
content:
President of the Dangote Group, Alhaji Aliko Dangote, has berate Nigeria power generation output of between 4,500 to 5,000 MW, stating that the country should not be generating lower than 60,000 MW, if his conglomerate alone can produce over 1,500 megawatts for internal use.

“We as a company alone are producing, group-wide for our own consumption, over 1,500 MW. So, Nigeria should not be three times what we are producing as a country. Nigeria should be at about 50,000 MW to 60,000 MW. All this can be replicated in our power sector. There’s no reason why Nigeria should be doing 5,000 MW.

“What we have actually done here is much more difficult than making Nigeria 25,000 or 30,000 megawatts of power, with transmission and distribution. But it’s not the work of government alone.

“We have already asked the government to leave the sector. It’s supposed to be privatised. They have privatised it.

“We, the private sector, Nigerians, most especially us, should stop taking our money abroad and invest the money here to make sure that we develop our own country and continent, because without us showing the confidence that, yes, we have confidence in our own economy and the leadership of the country, foreigners will not come.

“We know our leaders; we have confidence in them. So, that money they’re taking out of the country, they should leave it here so that it can benefit everybody.

“I keep saying this: there’s nowhere that you will say that there’s no corruption. There are lots of countries that have more corruption than we do, but they are growing. Our biggest problem and challenge is that people who have stolen money have taken the money abroad.

“So, the money has no use to them; it has no use to their family because they cannot show their family that they have stolen money. And they are not investing here to grow the domestic economy,” he said.

title: Meta Deletes 10 Million Fake Profiles, And 500,000 Spam Accounts
content:
Meta, the parent company of Facebook, announced that it’s has removal over 10 million fake profiles and 500,000 spam accounts in the first half of 2025.

The clampdown also saw recycle or repost content from others users without permission or meaningful changes lose access to monetisation tools, and reduction in their content reach on Facebook feeds.

“We’re making progress. In the first half of 2025, we took action on around 500,000 accounts engaged in spammy behaviour or fake engagement. We also removed about 10 million profiles impersonating large content producers,” Meta stated.

To support genuine creators, Meta said: “Pages and profiles that post mostly original content tend to enjoy wider distribution across Facebook. Simply stitching clips together or adding a watermark will no longer count as meaningful editing. Content that provides real value and tells an authentic story is likely to perform better.

“Post-level insights to the Professional Dashboard, allowing content creators to track the performance of their posts has been added. Creators can now check their Support Home screen to see if they are at risk of facing restrictions on their posts or earnings.”

title: In Two Months, Tiktok Deletes Over 3.6 Million Nigerian Videos, Removed 129 Accounts
content:
Due to policy violation, TikTok has removed more than 3.6 million videos of Nigeria users from its platform between January and March 2025 for breaching its Community Guidelines,

According to the report on Tuesday, TikTok achieved a proactive detection rate of 98.4 per cent, meaning most of the videos were removed before users reported them. About 92.1 per cent of the videos were taken down within 24 hours of being uploaded.

As part of its regional enforcement actions, TikTok also removed 129 accounts in West Africa linked to covert operations in March 2025, and hint on its intensify efforts to monitor LIVE broadcasts to ensure compliance with its rules. In the first quarter of 2025, the platform banned 42,196 LIVE rooms and interrupted 48,156 streams in Nigeria found to have violated its guidelines.

TikTok also announced new initiatives which comprised the expansion of its in-app helpline to Nigeria, in partnership with Cece Yara, a child-focused non-profit organisation that supports youth safety. The helpline will provide expert assistance to young users dealing with issues like suicide, self-harm, hate, and harassment.

They also named Dr. Olawale Ogunlana, popularly known as Doctor Wales, as its Digital Well-being Ambassador for Nigeria, joining a group of healthcare professionals in the WHO Fides Network.

Globally, TikTok removed over 211 million videos in Q1 2025, up from 153 million in the previous quarter. Of these, 184 million were removed through automation, with a global proactive detection rate of 99 per cent.

title: Marketers Protest As Dangote Intend To Crash Price Of Cooking Gas
content:
President of the Dangote Group, Alhaji Aliko Dangote, during a recent tour in his refinerywith some local and foreign guests, has hinted on the plan to reduce the current price of cooking gas to make it more affordable to the citizens, stating that its expensive and not affordable for the common people who depend on firewood for cooking.

He also promised to start direct sales of the product to consumers should the existing distributors fail to allow the price crash in cooking gas.

However, operators in the sector have disagreed with the plan, saying the businessman was planning to monopolise the LPG sector, saying market should be protected to encourage growth, and that collaborative efforts should be encourage which has grew Nigeria gas sector from 70,000 metric tonnes in 2007 to over 1.3 million tonnes in 2022.

“The one that we didn’t write, which you must have seen, is LPG. Currently, we do LPG of about 2,000 tonnes per day. You know Nigeria is gradually moving to the usage of LPG. But I believe it is expensive, but right now we’re trying to bring down the price and make it cheaper.

“If the distributors are not trying to bring it down, we’ll go directly and sell to the consumers, so that people will now transit from firewood or kerosene to LPG for cooking,” Dangote said.

On their part, the former Chairman of the LPG and Natural Gas Downstream Group of the Lagos Chamber of Commerce and Industry, Godwin Okoduwa, described the plan as monopolistic.

“I think it’s monopolistic. I think a market should be protected to encourage growth. The LPG industry in Nigeria grew from 70,000 metric tonnes in 2007 to over 1.3 million tonnes in 2022. That was done by collaboration — collaboration with the Federal Government, the NLNG, and offtakers. Everything was done in collaboration. It grew from 70,000 to 250 to 800, and now over a million.
