title: AWVCC25: Women’s African Volleyball Club Championship 39th Edition Match Day one event, glamour
content:
April 3, 2025, marks the official opening ceremony of the highly anticipated competition by the Grand Patron of the championship, the First Lady of the Federal Republic of Nigeria, Senator Oluremi Tinubu, CON which also has dignitaries and sports enthusiasts from across Africa present at the Moshood Abiola National Stadium, Abuja.

Hundreds of fans packed into Mushood Abiola Sport Indoor Hall on the evening to witness the official opening ceremony of the continent’s most prestigious event for clubs, hosting in Nigeria for the second time since its creation.

The night was graze with music, dance, art and culture as fans wept and bowed their heads with the emotion of the moment.

Sixteen clubs from ten African countries are participating in this year tournament.

The first game of the day was between Rwandan APR vs Carthage of Tunisia, before host Nigeria Customs take on Mayo Kane Evolution of Cameroun in straight sets 3-0 win in Pool A.

It was Carthage of Tunisia that first taste the victory against Rwandan APR with 25-18 score sheet in the first set of the opening game before a shocking come-back from the later with 26-24, 25-23, 25-23 to coast in the victory that will go down in the history books.

In the other Pool A encounter, host Nigeria Customs had an easy show against the young Mayo Kane Evolution of Cameroun in straight sets 3-0 (25-18, 25-17, 25-22) victory in front home fans.

NCS took the first set 25-18 with quick movement and distribution of the ball around the court. The home team played some excellent defence on the backcourt to save a number of balls. It was not difficult for the host in the second set contesting every point. A number of hitting and serving mistakes from both teams didn’t change how close it was. NSC took the last few points to win 25-17.

NCS scored early and led for the set, playing some smart points. Consistent recycling of the ball led to well-earned points winning the third set with a tight margin of 25-22 win, as the crowd went wild in support for Customs. The presence of the First Lady at some point and the Controller General throughout the game also high the morale of the Nigeria team.

title: Nearly Three Decades, Nigeria Returns to Spotlight as Tinubu set to Declare Open 2025 WAVC Champs
content:
On Wednesday, the giant of Africa played host to the 16th Women’s African Volleyball Club Championship (AWVCC25) after almost three decades. The tournament which set to feature sixteen teams across Africans from April 1st-April 14th will be hosted at the multipurpose sports hall of the Moshood Abiola National Stadium in the Federal Capital Territory.

Today, Thursday, April 4, 2025, marks the official opening ceremony of the highly anticipated competition by the Grand Patron of the championship, the First Lady of the Federal Republic of Nigeria, Senator Oluremi Tinubu, CON. Dignitaries and sports enthusiasts from across Africa will be present at the Moshood Abiola National Stadium, Abuja, to join the tournament official declaration.

Excitement is building in Abuja as final preparations are being made. A technical meeting which was held on Wednesday night, the organizers reaffirmed their commitment to hosting a successful tournament.

Speaking at the technical meeting, the host, Comptroller General of the Nigeria Customs Service (CGC), Adewale Adeniyi MFR, described the event as the Greatest Assembly of Volleyball in Africa, while assured all participants a memorable experience during and after the tournament.

“It is our pleasure to welcome the greatest assembly of volleyball in Africa to Abuja, Nigeria. We are truly delighted to have you here.

“When you watch a volleyball game, you see 12 players on the court, maybe two or three officials. But behind the scenes, the value chain extends much further the umpires, referees, scorers, statisticians, and everyone involved in making the tournament a success. We are honored to host you all.

“I have been involved in a few of these tournaments before, but in different capacities. This is the first time we are playing the role of host, and we are committed to making your stay in Nigeria enjoyable,” he said.

The President of the Nigeria Volleyball Federation (NVBF), Engr. Musa Nimrod, also said “We wish all the teams the best of luck during their stay in Abuja,” in his welcoming address.

title: River State Politics: my wife is reading script — Ex-Rivers HoS denied wife claims
content:
The Former Rivers State Head of Service, Dr.  George Nwaeke, in a video released in the early hours of Saturday has dismissed his wife claims of been kidnapped or coerced, suggesting that she had been misled and given a script to read.

Recalls, Mrs. Florence Nwaeke, wife of the former Head of Service in Rivers State, after saw an online interview granted by her husband, stated, that is not her husband, and that the interview is suspicious.

“When he got to Abuja, he called that he had landed. I said, Thank God. But when I saw the online interview granted by my husband, I said ‘That is not my husband. That is not my husband.’

“So I sent him a message. I said, ‘Are you under duress?’ I sent him a message. I said, ‘Have they kidnapped you? Talk to me now. Why are you not talking to me?

“Oh, Jesus, help me. Nigerians, help me. My husband is in trouble. My husband is in trouble. My husband is in trouble. My husband is in trouble. Look at the message I sent to him. See the message I sent to him. I said, ‘Daddy, why? Were you in hostage?’ I said, ‘Why didn’t you talk to me?’ These are the messages I sent to him, but he didn’t reply to me. His numbers are not going through. Nigerians, help me! Nigerians, help me!

“Governor, help me. My husband is in trouble. He is in trouble,” she said while appeals to Nigerians and embattle Gov Fubara, claiming her husband resigned under duress.

Dr. Nwaeke contrary to his wife assertion said, he is safe in Abuja where he had gone to voluntarily report himself to security agencies over developments in Rivers State.

“I am in TRANSCORP Abuja. I arrived this morning from Port Harcourt to meet security agencies and report myself, as well as the troubling events happening in Rivers State. I resigned as Head of Service on Monday because of these developments.

“I just saw a video of my wife trending. She was told I had been kidnapped and given a script to read. I want to make it clear—I am not kidnapped. I am in Abuja, working.

“When I was Head of Service, my wife was not involved in my official duties. That script she read is null and void. I am safe and sound. I will report myself to the appropriate security agencies because Abuja houses their headquarters, and I feel safer making my report here,” he said.

I want to tell the people of Rivers State today that the House of Assembly Complex on Moscow Road was deliberately brought down by Edison Ehie under the instructions of Governor Siminalayi Fubara. He also shared screenshots of alleged chats between Nwaeke and his Chief of Staff, Edison Ehie, in which Nwaeke reportedly sought financial support.

However, Florence Nwaeke, wife of the former Head of Service in Rivers State, after saw the online interview granted by her husband, stated, that is not her husband, and that the interview is suspicious.

“When he got to Abuja, he called that he had landed. I said, Thank God. But when I saw the online interview granted by my husband, I said ‘That is not my husband. That is not my husband.’

“So I sent him a message. I said, ‘Are you under duress?’ I sent him a message. I said, ‘Have they kidnapped you? Talk to me now. Why are you not talking to me?

“Oh, Jesus, help me. Nigerians, help me. My husband is in trouble. My husband is in trouble. My husband is in trouble. My husband is in trouble. Look at the message I sent to him. See the message I sent to him. I said, ‘Daddy, why? Were you in hostage?’ I said, ‘Why didn’t you talk to me?’ These are the messages I sent to him, but he didn’t reply to me. His numbers are not going through. Nigerians, help me! Nigerians, help me!”

title: PDP Crisis: Another Deputy Gov candidate resigns from the party
content:
In a letter dated March 28, 2025, and addressed to the chairman of Edem Odo Ward in Akpabuyo Local Government Area, Dr Emana Ambrose-Amawhe, the Peoples Democratic Party’s (PDP) deputy governorship candidate in the 2023 general election in Cross River State has tendered her resignation from the party, expected to be effective immediately.

She was the running mate to Senator Sandy Onor in the 2023 governorship election in Cross River.

 “I am writing to formally resign my membership from the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) with immediate effect.

”I sincerely appreciate the opportunity given to me over time to contribute my quota to the growth of the party and the chance to serve as the Deputy Governorship Candidate in the last general elections.

”It was a privilege to be part of the PDP’s vision and engage with our people in meaningful ways. However, after much reflection in light of the current state of affairs within the party, I believe it is time for me to move on.

“This decision was not made lightly, but I remain committed to serving my community and contributing to the progress of our state and nation in other capacities,” she said in the letter.

Dr Emana had also contested for the House of Representatives seat for the Bakassi/Akpabuyo/Calabar South Federal Constituency under the PDP.

title: 2026 World Cup Qualifier: Hope Rises As South Africa Faces Three-point Deduction for misconduct
content:
Momentums are gathering in Super Eagles group C to qualify for the 2026 FIFA World Cup as South Africa faces a three-point deduction following fielding of ineligible player Teboho Mokoena against Zimbabwe in matchday 4 of the World Cup qualifier.

Mokoena, the Mamelodi Sundowns midfielder was also booked in the 52nd minute during their 3-1 win over Zimbabwe in June 2024.

Despite the two yellow cards which rendered him ineligible he was named in South Africa matchday 5 tie against Lesotho last Friday.

According to FIFA World Cup qualifying rules, a player is ineligible to play a subsequent match after accumulating two yellow cards.

"If players or team officials receive two cautions in one match (in matches decided by penalties) or in two different matches of the competition, they will be automatically suspended from their team’s subsequent match.

"Protests regarding the eligibility of players selected for matches in the preliminary competition shall be submitted in writing to the FIFA Match Commissioner within two hours of the match in question and followed up with a full written report, including a copy of the original protest, to be submitted to the FIFA Disciplinary Committee in accordance with the applicable provisions of the FIFA Disciplinary Code and by email to qualifiers@fifa.org within 24 hours of the end of the match and shall be dealt with by the FIFA Disciplinary Committee, otherwise, they will be disregarded."

This implies that Mokoena should not have participated in the Lesotho match. Additionally, the code clarifies that “cautions received during one competition are not carried over to another competition,” meaning his yellow cards from World Cup qualifiers were not reset by playing in AFCON qualifiers.

However, for disciplinary action to be taken, FIFA’s regulations require that protests be submitted in writing to the Disciplinary Committee within 24 hours of the match.

The complaint must be based on the participation of an ineligible player who failed to meet FIFA’s eligibility requirements. In such cases, FIFA’s judicial body “may impose any appropriate disciplinary measures.”

However, since Lesotho did not file a formal protest, it remains uncertain whether FIFA will take action on its own.

title: World Cup Qualifier: Super Eagles’ Hopes After Draw With Zimbabwe
content:
Nigeria’s hopes of reaching the 2026 FIFA World Cup finals suffered a setback on Tuesday after a last-minute equalizer from the Warriors of Zimbabwe in their Matchday 6 encounter at the Godswill Akpabio Stadium in Uyo.

The result saw Super Eagles World Cup hopes take a hit after failing to secure a crucial victory against Zimbabwe. They needed a win to stay on track for qualification but could only manage a 1-1 draw in Uyo.

This means the Super Eagles are still stuck in fourth place with 7 point in group C behind the group leaders South Africa after defeated Benin Republic 2-0 in Abidjan that took them to 13 points.

After a goalless first half, striker Victor Osimhen broke the deadlock in the 74th minute. Before been forced off due to injury and replaced by Victor Boniface. However, Zimbabwe seized momentum after his exit and found a dramatic equalizer in the 90th minute, silencing the home crowd. 

Benin Republic’s Cheetahs and Rwanda’s Amavubi are both on eight points, one more than the Super Eagles, with four rounds of matches left, to be played over the months of September and October.

title: Impeachment: High Court Affirms Former Lagos FA Chairman Sack
content:
In March 2024, the Lagos State Football Association’s Congress passed a vote of no confidence against it’s former Chairman Fouad Oki, with 13 out of 14 congress members votes for his removal for an allege of unilaterally altering the Lagos State Football Association’s (LSFA) existing statutes, which negatively impacted the sport in the state.

Mr. Oki approach the Lagos High Court for an appeal, seeking to be reinstated I order to finish his term after 10 months in office. The prayers which was rejected by the Court, as Justice Olalekan A. Oresanya rules that the suit lacked merit. 

According to Justice Olalekan, "The Nigeria Football Federation (NFF), being the supervising authority of the Extra Ordinary General Assembly of the Lagos State Football Association (LSFA) is a necessary party to the suit.

“The Extra Ordinary General Assembly of the Lagos State Football Association (LSFA) not being a personal act of the defendants/applicants, the defendants/applicants cannot be personally sued as done in this case.

"This suit cannot be effectively decided without the Nigeria Football Federation (NFF) and its affliate, the Lagos State Football Association (LSFA) being made parties.

"The claimant cannot maintain this action against the defendants/applicants as sued in their personal capacity over their official act as Congress Members of the Lagos State Football Association (LSFA) is an agency of the Federal Government, this court has no jurisdiction to hear letters relating to their interpretation of the articles in their statutes.

"The Nigeria Football Federation (NFF) being an agency of the Federal Government, the High Court of Lagos State, has no jurisdiction over this matter. 

"This suit has not been properly brought against the defendants/applicants in accordance with the statutes of the NFF and LSFA statutes and the rules of this court.

title: World Cup Qualifier: It's Not Over Yet, Zimbabwe’s Incentive Won’t Stop Us – gladiators speaks
content:
In an effort to boost their chances of qualify for the 2026 world cup, the Zimbabwean government, after its national team ‘the Warriors’ secured a hard-fought 2-2 draw on Thursday against Benin Cheetahs in a match played in South Africa, has pledged a $150,000 cash reward for the team if they defeat the Super Eagles at the Godswill Akpabio Stadium in Uyo on Tuesday.

 William Troost-Ekong, the Super Eagles assistant captain, while speaking upon the team's arrival from Rwanda, acknowledged the incentive but remained confident in Nigeria’s determination to win. He dismissed Zimbabwe’s financial motivation, asserting that it won’t deter Nigeria from securing victory

"We read somewhere that the Zimbabweans are being motivated to come to Uyo and get a result. They should forget it.

"Our biggest motivation is the ambition to play at the FIFA World Cup. Apart from myself, Alex (Iwobi), and maybe a couple of others who played in 2018, this generation is hungry to compete at the highest level. We want to make Nigeria proud and, at the same time, do ourselves proud," Ekong told thenff.com.

On his part, the Chairman Senate Committee on Sports, Senator Abdul Ahmed Ningi says "It's Not Over Yet" has he tasks Super Eagles to remain focused and not to allow distraction set in as they host Zimbabwe next Tuesday in Uyo.

"I want to congratulate all the players and officials of Super Eagles on their victory in Kigali after beating Rwanda 2-0 to get their win in the qualifier. This reignited the hopes of Nigeria flag being hoisted in the 2026 FIFA World Cup.

"I want to call their attention to another important match coming up next week against Zimbabwe in Uyo. All hands must be on the deck by being focused and go into the match with same enthusiasm and commitment as they approached Rwanda game.

"With victory against Zimbabwe in Nigeria, then the dream of qualifying for the world cup is beginning to become reality." He said.

The Super Eagles is in fourth position in the group C with six points while South Africa lead with 10 points, Benin Republic are second with 8 points, and Rwanda are placed third with seven points.

title: World Cup Race: Super Eagles, and the Warriors of Zimbabwe Touchdown Uyo Ahead Of Tuesday Clash
content:
In continuation of the 2026 FIFA World Cup qualifiers, Zimbabwe’s national team, the Warriors, and the Nigeria Super Eagle team have arrived in Uyo, Akwa Ibom State ahead of their Tuesday crucial World Cup qualifiers match at the Godswill Akpabio International Stadium Uyo.

The Nigerian national team landed at the Victor Attah International Airport, Uyo at exactly 2:15pm on Saturday from Kigali after a successful outing where they defeated Rwanda 2-0 with Victor Osimhen's brace which move them to 6 point. 4 point behind South africa, the table leader

Zimbabwe, after secured a hard-fought 2-2 draw on Thursday against Benin Cheetahs in a match played in South Africa landed in Lagos on Saturday morning before taking a connecting flight to Uyo for the upcoming encounter.

The highly anticipated clash between Nigeria and Zimbabwe is set to take place at the Godswill Akpabio Stadium in Uyo on Tuesday.

title: President Tinubu’s appointee labels Arise TV journalist “IPOB girl”
content:
Mr Ayo Oyalowo, a President Bola Tinubu appointee as one of the directors of the Ogun-Osun River Basin Development Authority, in a tweet on Friday, has labelled an Arise TV journalist  Ojy Okpe as an “IPOB girl.”  

Oyalowo,made the remark when reacting to an edition of Arise Morning Show where Oseni Rufai and Ms Okpe accused TVC’s Babajide Otitoju of double mouth regarding president Tinubu’s declaration of a state of emergency in Rivers State. Initially, they said he opposed the declaration but later supporting the move after it was officially announced.

Ms Okpe, during the show  raised Mr Otitoju’s previous statement as against his new stands on the subject matter, the action Mr Rufai referred to as double-speak of the TVC’s journalist.

“Rufai and that stupid IPOB girl think they can rubbish @BabajideOtitoju because they work for an ambush TV? Are they mad or what?

“Is Jide their mate both in age and in experience? This is insanity taken too far, and I will personally be mad at Jide if he lets this rubbish slide,”  Oyalowo stated.

On his part, Mr Otitoju debunked the accusation, has he called it an “open lie” against his personality. 

“There is nothing like taking back what I said. Reading the Constitution, I was convinced that the president has no power to suspend democratic structures. It is borderline irresponsibility for anybody to say Jide took back what he said.

“No TV station in Nigeria can rubbish the name I have made. I was forged in the fire of qualitative journalism. I was trained by the best. Some of the people at the TV stations that openly lied against me—some of their best in that station—passed through me,” Mr Otitoju said.

title: UPDATES: LP And PDP Lawmakers Berate Obi, Atiku, Support Tinubu Decision
content:
The Senate in a resolution on Thursday’s during closed-door session has approved the state of emergency imposed on Rivers State by President Bola Tinubu on Tuesday., which  suspend Governor Siminalayi Fubara, his deputy, Ngozi Odu, and other elected officials.

Senate leader, Opeyemi Bamidele, moved a motion for a closed session under Order 135 of the Senate rules to deliberate on the matter awhich was seconded by the Senate Minority Leader, Abba Moro, after Senate President, Godswill Akpabio, read a letter from Tinubu seeking for approval of the declaration at plenary on Thursday.

After voice vote, Akpabio stated that the Senate had exercised its powers under Section 305(2) of the Constitution and endorse the president’s proclamation.

“We hope that the President’s declaration will foster peace and resolve the ongoing impasse in Rivers State,” Akpabio remarked.

Additionally, the Senate urged Tinubu to establish an ad hoc committee composed of “eminent” Nigerians to mediate between the warring factions in Rivers State.

The lawmakers also decided that the President should review or terminate the state of emergency at any time, but no later than six months from now.

Furthermore, the Senate agreed to authorise the formation of an ad hoc committee, with members from both chambers of the National Assembly, to oversee the situation in the state.

Earlier, Peter Obi, the presidential aspirant of Labour Party in the 2023 general election charge LP Lawmakers to vote against the president Tinubu declaration.

On his X, he wrote: “My dear brothers and sisters, Members of the Labour Party in the National Assembly, Since your inauguration as Distinguished, and Honorable members of the National Assembly, I have refrained from interfering in your legislative affairs out of respect for your independence and to allow you to focus on alleviating the suffering of the Nigerian people.

“However, at this critical juncture — following 26 years of a deteriorating democratic process marked by disregard for educational qualifications for electoral positions, massive rigging, and now the unconstitutional removal of elected officeholders — I find it necessary to address you.

“These unconstitutional actions have far-reaching negative implications for our democracy and the will of the people.

“I urge you to stand as true defenders of justice. Do not participate in or support any action, decision, or vote that compromises the integrity of our democracy, undermines the interests of the people of Rivers State, or contradicts our core values of fairness, equity, and transparency.

“We must not allow ourselves to become instruments of injustice or contribute to the betrayal of the people's mandate. At this moment, we must prioritize what is right over what is wrong or convenient, remaining steadfast in defending the well-being of the people of Rivers State. Together, let us stand firm in our resolve — because a new Nigeria is possible!”

Same as Atiku Abubakar of the PDP. As he wrote on his X account: “Immediately I left the Shehu Yar’Adua Centre where we had addressed a joint press conference of the Coalition of Opposition Political Parties in which we called for President Tinubu to reverse the declaration of a state of emergency rule in Rivers State; I spoke to a former Governor of Rivers, His Excellency Chief Rufus Ada-George. At the time we spoke, Ada-George was presiding over a meeting of the Rivers Elders and Leaders Forum. I impressed on him the need for them to reach out to the lawmakers from the region to vote against the proclamation of state of emergency rule in Rivers State.”

title: 2026 World Cup: NFF Rallies Support For Super Eagles As They Aim Six Points Against Rwanda, Zimbabw
content:
The Nigeria Football Federation (NFF) has called on all Nigerians for their support towards the  national team, Super Eagle in the upcoming 2026 World Cup qualifiers against Rwanda, Zimbabwe as they aim for maximum point.

As contained in the communique issued at the end of NFF Executive Committee meeting held on Monday in Abuja. NFF charged the Super Eagles to pick the maximum points against their opponents. While calls on well-meaning Nigerians to support and encourage the team in whatever fair and proper way to guarantee victory in both matches.

Nigeria will confront group C leaders Rwanda in Kigali on Friday, 21st March, before taking on Zimbabwe’s Warriors at the Godswill Akpabio Stadium, Uyo, four days later.

"the Executive Committee charged the players to go all out for the six points in both matches to boost Nigeria’s qualification hopes. It also called on all Nigerians to support and encourage the team in whatever fair and proper way they are competent to, in order to guarantee victory in both matches."

“Adequate preparations have been put in place to ensure a successful outings for the team. Proper logistics and general support services have been put in place for the Super Eagles ahead of their upcoming 2026 FIFA World Cup qualifying matches against Rwanda in Kigali (Friday, 21st March) and Zimbabwe in Uyo (Tuesday, 25th March)," the communique reads.

The match against  group C leaders Rwanda in Kigali will be the first game for the  Head Coach, Éric Sékou Chelle, as the Super Eagles' new manager.

title: Transfer Update: Galatasaray VP Kavukcu, reveals Osimhen Future and decision
content:
The Nigerian Super Eagle striker, Victor Osimhen who is on  loan at Galatasaray's  in Turkey from Serie A side Napoli last season will make a decision on his future in April said Galatasaray's Vice President, Abdullah Kavukcu.

Osimhen has been the subject of intense transfer speculation following his outstanding performances for the Turkish Super Lig champions since joining Galatasaray's, prompting the club to push for a permanent deal.

However, they face stiff competition from European giants such as Chelsea, Manchester United, and Arsenal.

 "Osimhen will inform us of his decision next month. At the moment, five of the world's biggest clubs are also interested in him.

 "In January, there were discussions about his departure, but he chose to stay. He loves Galatasaray very much.

"Although our focus is on the title race, we haven't had direct talks with Victor yet. There's no point in discussing it now.

 "Galatasaray is a top club. If that weren’t the case, Victor wouldn’t have come here. Keeping him isn’t impossible,” Kavukcu told journalist Nevzat Dindar.

title: Construction of NFF-FIFA Players’ Hostel and new Training Pitches inside MKO Abiola Stadium commence
content:
The Speaker of the House of Representatives, Rt. Hon. Tajudeen Abbas, GCON, on Tuesday cut the tape on the epitaph, which signalled the commencement of work on the NFF-FIFA Players’ Hostel and new Training Pitches located inside the MKO Abiola National Stadium, Abuja.

On a sunny spring afternoon in Nigeria’s administrative capital, eminent personalities in the political, business and football sectors showed genuine excitement at a transformational project that is sure to boost the stock of the Ibrahim Gusau-led NFF administration with football stakeholders and enthusiasts at home and abroad.

“This is a noble project and the National Assembly will give it full support. I congratulate the National Sports Commission and the Nigeria Football Federation, and I thank FIFA for agreeing to fund this project,” Rt. Hon. Abbas said as he cut the tape.

Lead of the FIFA team, Gelson Fernandes (Deputy Chief Member Associations Officer/Regional Director, Africa) said FIFA was happy to provide funds for the project as infrastructure development is at the heart of FIFA’s vision since the coming into office of President Gianni Infantino.

An elated Gusau stated that the facilities will serve all the various national teams: “Indeed, my joy knows no bounds as this is one of the projects that I was determined to push with my Executive Committee to bequeath as a legacy to Nigeria football, right from the day we were sworn into office in Benin City on Friday, 30th September 2022.

“For sustained success, it is imperative for us to provide the conducive environment, infrastructure, equipment and support systems that will allow the players and officials to give their very best at all times, and compete favourably at the highest level...building a players' hostel and having new training pitches, that can serve the national teams, leagues and academies, will not only enhance team management, it will surely reduce expenditure in these areas and enable us to commit more funds to grassroots development programs.”  

There were goodwill messages by Chairman of the National Sports Commission, Alhaji Shehu Dikko, who incidentally played a key role in the actualization of the old FIFA Goal Project that included the Technical Centre and the synthetic pitch, which will now be reconstructed, as well as securing the land space for the new project; Comptroller-General of the Nigeria Customs Service, CG Bashir Adeniyi; former Edo State deputy governor Phillip Shaibu; Chairman of the Senate Committee on Sports, Senator Abdul Ningi; former youth and sports minister, Chief Sunday Dare (now the SA, Media and Public Communications/Spokesperson to Mr. President and Commander-In-Chief of the Armed Forces) and; Nigeria legend Olusegun Odegbami, who spoke on behalf of legends present.

The Ambassador of UAE to Nigeria, His Excellency Salem Ali Shamsi attended, as well as former sports minister, Senator John Owan Enoh (now Minister of State for Industry); NFF 2nd VP Hon. Gbenga Elegbeleye and Executive Committee members Yusuf Ahmed, Sharif Rabiu Inuwa, Babagana Kalli, Sunday Dele-Ajayi, Aisha Falode, Ganiyu Majekodunmi, Margaret Icheen, Ali Silas Agara, Nse Essien, George Aluo and Timothy Magaji and; NFF General Secretary, Dr. Mohammed Sanusi.

Former NFF General Secretary, Ambassador Fanny Amun was present, with FIFA officials El Hadj Diop and Nataniel Nascimento Brito; NFF congressmen Mohammed Mouktar and Faisal Abdullahi and; legends Mutiu Adepoju, Samson Siasia, Victor Ikpeba, Precious Dede and Stella Mbachu.

Nigeria’s Chief of Defence Staff, General Christopher Musa, the Inspector General of Police, Dr Kayode Egbetokun, the Ambassador of Morocco to Nigeria and the Chairman of the House of Reps’ Committee on Sports were represented.

NFF

title: State of Emergency: Fubara Released Statement… Strength or weakness?
content:
Suspended Rivers State Governor, Siminalayi Fubara, in a statement he personally signed and made available on Wednesday, has urged the people of the state to remain calm in the face of the political impasse in the state. Stating that all his actions and decisions have been guided by his constitutional oath of office and a great sense of duty.

“I address you today with a deep sense of responsibility and calm, as we navigate this unfortunate moment in our state’s political history. Since assuming office as your governor, we have prioritised the protection of lives and property and ensured the continuous progress of our dear state.

“Even in the face of the political impasse, we have remained committed to constitutional order and the rule of law, putting the interest of our people above all else.

“This was why, immediately after Mr. President’s intervention to broker peace, we did not hesitate to implement the agreed terms in good faith, including welcoming back commissioners who had previously resigned of their own volition.

“Furthermore, we moved swiftly to comply with the Supreme Court’s judgment immediately after we received the certified true copy of the judgment to return the state to normalcy.

“Unfortunately, at every turn, members of the Rivers State House of Assembly frustrated our efforts, thus making genuine peace and progress challenging.

“Our priorities remained the security of lives and property and advancing the well-being and prosperity of Rivers people.

“Yes, we have political disagreements, but good governance had continued, salaries have been paid, and great projects were being executed to move the State forward. Above all, Rivers State is safe, secure, and peaceful under our watch.

“At this critical time, I urge all Rivers people to remain peaceful and law-abiding. We will engage with all relevant institutions to ensure that our democracy remains strong and that Rivers State continues to thrive. We have always been resilient people, and we will face this situation with wisdom, patience, and unwavering faith in the democratic process,” he stated as report by Punch online.

On March 18, 2025, President Bola Tinubu declared a state of emergency in Rivers State following the protracted political crisis in the state.

Tinubu made the proclamation during a nationwide broadcast on Tuesday, suspending Governor Siminalayi Fubara; his deputy Ngozi Odu; and all the members of the House of Assembly for six months.

The president nominated Vice Admiral Ibokette Ibas (rtd) as administrator to take charge of the affairs of the state for the first six months.

title: President Tinubu has officially sent a letter to NASS for approval of declared state of emergency
content:
President Bola Tinubu has officially sent a letter to the House of Representatives, requesting their approval for declaring a state of emergency in Rivers State.

On March 18, 2025, President Bola Tinubu declared a state of emergency in Rivers State following the protracted political crisis in the state.

Tinubu made the proclamation during a nationwide broadcast on Tuesday, suspending Governor Siminalayi Fubara; his deputy Ngozi Odu; and all the members of the House of Assembly for six months.

The president nominated Vice Admiral Ibokette Ibas (rtd) as administrator to take charge of the affairs of the state for the first six months.

Akin Rotimi, the spokesperson for the House of Representatives, acknowledged the development.

“The leadership of the National Assembly met with Mr. President and the National Security Adviser ahead of the broadcast.

“Key security chiefs were also present and were fully briefed on the situation. All parties unanimously expressed their support.

“The letter will be read on the floor of the House during plenary on Wednesday, March 19, 2025.

“Further legislative action will be debated and decided on the floor," he said.

title: Tinubu Declared State of Emergency in River State Appoint New Administrator
content:
Present Tinubu on Tuesday has declared state of emergency in River State and appointed Vice Admiral Ibok-Ete Ekwe Ibas Rtd as the Administrator for the state, following political crisis rocking the state.

Before now the state house of Assembly has notified the Governor of gross misconduct which amount to impeachment. And just today explosion rock some oil pipeline though yet to be connected to the ongoing crisis but the militant had made the warning earlier.

Vice Admiral Ibok-Ete Ekwe Ibas, born on September 27, 1960, in Nko, Cross River State, Nigeria, is a distinguished Nigerian naval officer and diplomat. He served as the 22nd Chief of Naval Staff of the Nigerian Navy from July 2015 until his retirement in January 2021. In recognition of his exemplary service, he was appointed as Nigeria's Ambassador to Ghana in 2021.

Educational Background and Naval Training:

Ibas commenced his primary education at Nko Primary School and completed it at Big Qua Primary School, Calabar, in 1971. He attended Hope Waddell Training Institute from 1972 to 1976 and the School of Basic Studies, Ogoja, between 1977 and 1979. His naval career began at the Nigerian Defence Academy on June 20, 1979, as part of the 26th Regular Course, leading to his commission as a sub-lieutenant on January 1, 1983.

Throughout his career, Ibas pursued advanced military education, including:

- Sub-Lieutenant Technical Course at INS Venduruthy, India (1983-1984)

- Primary Pilot Training at the 301 Primary Flying Training School, Nigerian Air Force Base, Kaduna (1986-1987)

- Junior Staff Course at the Armed Forces Command and Staff College, Jaji (1990)

- Diploma in Amphibious Warfare from the U.S. Marine Corps University, Quantico, Virginia (1992-1993)

- Underwater Warfare specialization at the Underwater Warfare School, NNS Quorra (1994-1995)

- Senior Staff Course at the Armed Forces Command and Staff College, Jaji (1996-1997)

- National Defence Course at the National Defence College, Islamabad, Pakistan, earning a master's degree in defense and strategic studies from Quaid-i-Azam University (2005-2006)

Naval Career Highlights:

Ibas held numerous key positions within the Nigerian Navy, including:

- Executive Officer on NNS Siri, NNS Ekun, and NNS Ambe

- Commanding Officer of the Nigerian Navy Underwater Warfare School (1997-1998)

- Commander of the Forward Operating Base Ibaka (1998-2000)

- Directing Staff at the Armed Forces Command and Staff College, Jaji (2000-2002)

- Naval Provost Marshal (2003-2004)

- Principal Staff Officer to the Chief of Naval Staff (2004-2005)

- Command Operations Officer at the Western Naval Command Headquarters, Lagos (2006)

- Commander of the Naval Air Base, Ojo (2006-2009)

- Chief of Administration at Naval Headquarters (2011-2012)

- Navy Secretary (2012-2013)

- Flag Officer Commanding Western Naval Command (2013-2014)

- Chief of Logistics (2014)

- Group Managing Director/CEO of Nigerian Navy Holdings Limited (2014)

His tenure as Chief of Naval Staff from July 2015 to January 2021 was marked by significant contributions to Nigeria's maritime security and naval operations.

Diplomatic Role:

Following his retirement from active naval service, Ibas was appointed as Nigeria's Ambassador to Ghana in 2021, further extending his service to the nation in the diplomatic arena.

Personal Life:

Ibas is married to Barrister Theresa Ibas, and they are blessed with children. His personal interests include reading, watching documentaries, and playing golf.

Throughout his illustrious career, Vice Admiral Ibok-Ete Ekwe Ibas has exemplified dedication, leadership, and a commitment to the security and diplomatic interests of Nigeria.

title: corps member Ushie who criticised Tinubu is under serious pressure to apologise – Activists revealed
content:
The Human rights activist and publisher of Sahara Reporters, Omoyele Sowore, during an interview on Arise TV on Monday night has stated that the youth corps member Ushie Uguamaye who criticised President Bola Tinubu’s administration over hardship is under tremendous pressure to apologise from the likes of government officials including ministers.

Sowore, who accompanied the corps member to the NYSC Local Government Inspector’s office in Lagos with a team of lawyers, following an invitation from the NYSC, summoning her to appear before the LGI office at Eti Osa 3 on Monday, said the corps members committed no crime by exercising their freedom of expression in criticising Tinubu’s administration.

Recalls that on Saturday, a Lagos-based corp member, Uguamaye,  in a TikTok viral video  criticised President Bola Tinubu’s government, describing as “terrible leader”.

“I am coming from a supermarket where I went to get foodstuff, and everything has gone up again. It’s just like every single week, prices keep increasing.

“I want to know, what is the government doing about this increase? If a lot of Nigerians come out and start speaking about what we are going through, maybe changes will be made in the government.

“I don’t know if there is any other president that is as terrible as you (Mr Tinubu). But you (Mr Tinubu) are such a terrible president,” the corp member lamented.

Giving an update, the activist wrote: “We arrived at Eti-Osa LGI offices of the National Youth Service Corps with youth corper, Ushie Rita Uguamaye in Lagos. She was scheduled to appear before the LGI today and we escorted her to their offices with attorneys, Festus Ogun, Adeyinka Oyesomi and Ojienoh Justice but LGI officials had absconded failing to show up throughout our stay. We will be back! #RevolutionNow #tinubuisaterriblepresident.”

Meanwhile, another activist, and journalist, Agba Jalingo, urged Nigerians and authorities to show Uguamaye empathy and support instead of condemning her for the viral video.

In a Facebook post on Monday, Jalingo said Uguamaye experienced personal tragedy linked to poor government policies when her father, Raphael Ushie, a Chief Inspector of the Nigeria Immigration Service, died in May 2019 after protesting the demolition of his palm plantation for the Obudu International Airport project.

“There was a protest by youths and women of the Ukambi community over the demolition of their community farmlands for the Obudu International cargo and passenger airport.

“According to a CrossRiverWatch report, her dad, Ushie, who was also the younger brother of Governor Ayade’s physician, Dr Vincent Ushie, died after he was rushed from a hospital in Obudu to the University of Calabar Teaching Hospital, having participated in the protest.”

“Ushie, who was approaching retirement, had invested his life savings in a palm plantation in Ukambi. Upon hearing that demolitions had begun in neighbouring communities and were nearing Ukambi, he hurried home to protect his land.

“He arrived and went straight to the farm in his uniform and met the bulldozer nearing his plantation. He faced the operator and tried to prevent him from encroaching on his land before other community members joined him,” he wrote.

title: PDP attacks Jandor over return to APC
content:
The Lagos State chapter of the Peoples Democratic Party at a news conference on Monday in Lagos, has describe its governorship candidate in the 2023 general elections, Dr Abdul-Azeez Adediran, popularly known as Jandor, as an implant to destabilized the party following his return to the ruling All Progressives Congress.

Adediran, leader of the Lagos4Lagos Movement, who was previously a member of the APC before joining the PDP, announced his resignation from the PDP on March 3, 2025, citing a lack of discipline in the party and betrayal by its leaders.

Reacting to his defection in an interview with Punch correspondent on Monday, the Deputy Chairman of the PDP in Lagos, Tai Benedict, said Jandor was never “our own” and was allegedly planted by the APC to destabilize the PDP.

“He was never our own. He was an agent sent to our party to destroy our party. The very first time I saw him, I told him to explain – that you are an agent of the APC, sent to our party because they knew we had a bright chance to win that election.

“Although he denied it, eventually, I was vindicated. This was somebody who came to the party, and the first thing he did was to start accusing the leaders and the next thing he did was to disorganise a united party to the national level until he got the ticket of our party from the back.

“You know, it’s very unfortunate, very unfortunate. We have never had it so badly. But all I have to say is we thank God. We’re okay with his exit.

“He came, he singularly picked his running mate. It has never happened. He said because Funke (Akindele) had over three million followers on Instagram, that will make his victory (at the 2023 governorship poll) easier. But we had only 62,000 votes.”

“For me, I thank God that he has left our party. It’s not a good thing to lose membership in parties, I quite agree with that. It’s not good to lose your members to other parties. But there are some members that if they leave, you’ll be happy. One of such members is Jandor,” Benedict said.

Meanwhile, to the APC is a welcome development, as the party’s publicity secretary, Seye Oladejo, stated that, “Like all politicians, Jandor came to the party with ambition. At the time, that could be realised quickly on the platform of the conservatives, which has been rejected at the polls several times by the people of Lagos.

“So, now that he’s back, we’re happy to work with him. We appreciate the fact that Lagos has been better and safer in the hands of the progressives, who have enjoyed uninterrupted trust and confidence from the people.

“We believe in our party that there is sufficient opportunity for him, like many others, to contribute his quota to the continual success of our government and growth of our party.”

“Describing Jandor as implant to destabilize the opposition party is a shows of how inept ideas this so-called opposition is. In the days ahead, we’re expecting more decamps as we approach the next election

“We’re talking about a party that’s perpetually in crisis. We’re talking about a party that can’t organise itself, and they want to govern. The electorates in Lagos are informed, they are sophisticated.

“They’re just looking for excuses to justify their incompetence, and the fact that they’re incapable of mobilising whatever modicum of support they have for election victory.”

title: University of Port Harcourt To Introduce “Wikematics Political Ideology” Course in honour of Wike
content:
During a visit by the University of Port Harcourt Governing Council, led by the Pro-Chancellor and Chairman of the Council, Sen. Mao Ohuabunwa to the office of the  Federal Capital Territory (FCT) Minister, Mr Nyesom Wike, in Abuja on Monday, a promise has been made to introduce “Wikematics Political Ideology” as part of the studies at the Abuja centre if established, considering Wike’s political trajectory and antecedents in politics.

Mr. Wike promised to allocate land in the FCT to the University of Port Harcourt for the establishment of its Centre for Leadership and Political Studies, the request made by Ohuabunwa to the minister’s for his support to enable the university build the centre, a replica of the John F. Kennedy Leadership Center in America.

The Pro-Chancellor and Chairman of the Council who also sought Wike’s support to establish a well-equipped multimedia centre at the university’s Convocation Arena, to mark the university’s 50th anniversary stated that “Wikematics Political Ideology” would be part of the studies at the Abuja centre, if established to honour his antecedents in politics.

According to Ohuabunwa, the Convocation Arena was built by Wike when he was the governor of Rivers along with the Faculty of Law, which was established during his tenure as Minister of Education.

He also said that the university would celebrate its 50th anniversary in 2025 with a N10 billion endowment fund. And added that the minister would be among the distinguished alumni of the university to be celebrated at the event, considering his significant contributions to the university’s development.

The minister, who agreed to support the allocation of land, however, stated that he would not use FCT funds to build the centre.

He also pledged to support the university with N350 million, the amount it requested to build the multimedia centre, using money from his personal funds, as well as contributions from his wife and friends.

“Government alone cannot do it. Those of us who graduated from the university, and who God has helped, should also support.

“I cannot take FCT money and give it to you, no, but I will give you land to build your centre.

”My wife, my friends, and I will provide the money needed to build the multimedia centre you have asked for,” he said.

He also urged the university management to reach out to other alumni, particularly Gov. Charles Soludo of Anambra, who also graduated from the university.

(NAN)

title: My Key To Success At Galatasaray - Victor Osimhen
content:
The prolific forward, Nigeria's Super Eagles striker, Victor Osimhen, speaking after the match against Antalyaspor where he netted a stunning hat trick in Galatasaray’s dominant 4-0 victory has shared the secret behind his impressive form at his current club.

Osimhen who has been in best form this season, recording 26 goals and 5 assists across all competitions for Galatasaray, attributed his success to the strong bond within the team and praised his teammates for their contributions

"A big congratulations to the team and our fans—we deserved this win and did a great job," Osimhen said.

"Baris has been incredible, making us feel valued in recent matches. Yunus is back, and he’s a crucial player for us."

"We’ll work hard to build on this result in the coming games. Our team is built on love—we are brothers on and off the field."

title: Transfer Update: Atalanta Manager, Enrico, Streamline Lookman Transfer
content:
Atalanta manager Enrico Fedele, during a program on Tele A’s Fuorigioco as quoted by Area Napoli, has made it clear that Nigerian winger Ademola Lookman will not be joining Serie A rival.

"I’ve been in football for about fifty years and built many relationships. I can tell you that Napoli’s sporting director, Giovanni Manna, is targeting another player—Solet. Trust me, he’s really strong, very strong."

"Lookman to Napoli? No, there’s no chance this deal will happen. I don’t see why these rumours keep spreading," Fedele said on Tele A’s Fuorigioco program, as quoted by Area Napoli.

Lookman has been linked with a move away from the Gewiss Stadium at the end of the season, with top clubs like Napoli and Juventus showing interest in his services of which Fedele dismissed the possibility.

title: Abiola’s son: its needless Probing IBB over my father’s death
content:
Jamiu Abiola, the son of the late winner of the June 12, 1993 presidential election, Chief Moshood Abiola, in an interview with Sunday PUNCH has stated that prosecuting the former military Head of State, Ibrahim Babangida, over his father death is unnecessary. Stating that the time for such investigations had passed away, as many key figures involved in the tragedy are no longer alive.

“There is no need for prosecution or probe. So many years have passed and most of the good and bad actors in the June 12 tragedy have passed away.

“The appropriate time for a probe would have been during the second term of former President Olusegun Obasanjo, when Nigeria’s democracy was more stable and many individuals involved were still alive and could provide accurate accounts of events.

“The best way to compensate our family is for the Abiola family to see all Nigerians adopting the attitude they adopted on the day of June 12, 1993, which in a nutshell is to reject tribalism and religious differences when electing leaders and to see themselves as members of the same family regardless of their states of origin.

“By so doing they will be heeding the call of President Bola Tinubu to shun ethnicity and transforming Nigeria from a country to a nation.

“I will not ask for more than that because to do so would bring down the high standing of Moshood and Kudirat Abiola following their unique sacrifice. They gave up their lives and will be rewarded with more than 500 million years in a place better than any castle in this world.

“Any worldly honour given to them is definitely welcome, but believe it or not, it will be only a drop in the ocean compared to what they are enjoying right now and will continue enjoying while every single one of those who cheated and killed them burn in hell forever and ever by the special grace of God,” he stated.

Jamiu further stated that for those interested in knowing more with the goal of understanding the truth and not seeking revenge  should approach his book, The President Who Never Ruled

title: SA and UK based Nigerian Creative entrepreneur Launches platform for entertainment funding
content:
Fabian Lojede, a South Africa and UK based Nigerian creative entrepreneur, in a statement sent to Sunday Scoop, has announced the global launch of a platform, Prodculator, designed to streamline film tax incentives, financing, and investment matchmaking within the entertainment industry.

“As the global film industry continues to grow, navigating tax incentives and securing financing remains a major challenge for creatives, Prodculator is a game-changer, bridging the gap between film producers and funders while demystifying the complex world of tax rebates.

“Prodculator, established under DEO Media, aims to empower filmmakers, producers, and investors by allowing them to calculate tax rebates and connect with potential funders worldwide. For instance, a Nigerian filmmaker looking to shoot in South Africa or the UK can use the platform to calculate available tax rebates in those countries within minutes. While many African countries, including Nigeria, lack robust tax incentive programs, Prodculator offers creatives access to funding opportunities and helps investors discover projects to support. The platform also facilitates direct connections between filmmakers and investors interested in supporting productions through grants, rebates, and private financing.

“The platform will also benefits investors by making it easier to discover viable film projects. Prodculator provides a data-driven approach to identifying tax-efficient investments, offering transparency that allows financiers to support productions while maximising their returns through government incentives confidently.

“With this innovative tool, filmmakers now have an accessible, streamlined process to secure funding and navigate international tax rebates, giving them more opportunities to bring their creative visions to life while reaching a global audience. Other upcoming releases include Afrotods, a children-focused content platform, a soon-to-be-launched YouTube channel, and a creative masterclass platform, all set to launch later this year,” Lojede stated in the statement.

title: Emirate Tussle: Kano clarifies emir Sanusi’s reinstatement Appeal Court’s judgment
content:
Following the  recent Court of Appeal judgment regarding the ongoing controversy in the Kano emirship. The Kano State Government in a statement issued on Saturday by the Governor’s spokesman, Sunusi Dawakin-Tofa, during a press briefing held at the NUJ Secretariat in Kano, has made clarification concerning the widespread misinterpretations and speculative reports in the media.

The Kano State Attorney General and Commissioner for Justice, Haruna Dederi, while   speaking at the press briefing emphasised the need for accurate information regarding the legal proceedings.

“The Court of Appeal, in its judgment delivered on January 10, 2025, upheld the repeal of the Kano Emirate Council Law, 2019, and overturned the judgment of the Federal High Court, Kano.

“However, Alhaji Aminu Dan’agundi, dissatisfied with the verdict, and since filed an appeal before the Supreme Court of Nigeria.

“The recent stay of execution granted by the Court of Appeal as a standard legal procedure meant to maintain the status quo pending the determination of the case at the apex court.

“The Kano State Government urges the public to remain calm, law-abiding, and avoid any form of provocation.

“The government has also instructed its legal team to study the outcome of the proceedings and determine the next steps in line with the law,” the statement read.

title: Asake Responded To His Father viral video
content:
The Nigeria artist, Ahmed Babatunde Ololade Odunsin, popular know as Asake (Mr. Money) has reacted to the viral video of Mr. Fatai Odunsi, who claims to be his father.

Since the release of the video in the early hours of Friday, March 14 it has continue to stirred controversy on social media. In the video, Mr. Odunsi said: “I am Asake’s father. I gave birth to him. I gave birth to Asake, Ahmed, the singer. Babatunde Ololade Odunsin, Mr. Money. Since I had a stroke, I haven’t seen him. The last time I saw him was March 29, 2022. He doesn’t pick my calls when I call him. Please, I only need your help.

Some personalities who has direct contact with Asake or his father has also weigh in to the matter.

Tunde Phoenix, Asake’s ex-manager, in different posts while sharing his thought criticised the singer’s alleged abandonment of his father, writing, “Operation GoFundMe for your favorite’s Papa. Please help us find that old man, his seed won’t listen. He abandons people who have helped him. Even if they left you, should you act like them when God has blessed you beyond your wildest dreams? A heart of a man reveals all you need to know. Please find Papa, let’s get him the help he needs. These children have the audacity.

“One by one, God will show you who they are. Not my words anymore. Go and pick Papi up. We don’t care if he left as a child, in fact, I believe that man over anything you will say. If you don’t, we will handle your responsibilities for you and do a full interview with him to give us all the truths the masses want to know. You are a public figure. Get PR girl, put a statement together or I will. PS: PR girl is a vibe. Love her, I would definitely date her, she has a good heart but keeps bad company.”

Sulaimon Alade,  Asake’s former teacher also shares his perspectives on the family dispute as he recounted his past interactions with the artist and his father. “I was Asake’s teacher when he was in nursery school, right in front of my family house (Ile Atapupa or Ile Oni Gelede at No. 70 Ojuolokun Street, Isale Eko, Lagos). Back then, I worked with my brother, Musbau Teacher, the proprietor of MPS Mussey Private School. His father took good care of him as a single parent, dropping him off at school every morning. I swear with the Quran. After school, he would go to Agboolokun, his mother’s house, and stay there until evening when his dad (Malo) returned from work. I don’t know why he neglected his dad to this extent,” he wrote. 

Another testament was colleague of Asake father, Adetola Adunade Oso who said: “Fact. Malo took care of Ahmed (Asake). He never failed in his responsibilities as a father. We both worked with the Lagos Island Local Government—though in different departments—but maintained a cordial relationship until I retired in 2022. I can’t believe Ahmed could neglect his father in this state. I pray the Almighty Allah restores his health. So sad. Always smiling, Lammedah.”

Asake, responding to the allegation through a video, was seen singing in Yoruba, in an attempt to address the controversy. The lyrics of his song conveyed a message about staying true to himself despite external pressures. He sang, “You can’t please the world. Whatever you do, do it for God and always remember the day you’ll die and meet your God. My people, can you see how it’s going? Even my father wants to cajole me, but I stand firm and they can’t off my light. I used to press money for him and I do it with one mind. If you strike, I will move on. No one can quench my fire. God is the one that is taking me ahead in life.”

title: 2026 World Cup Race: Chelle names Ekong, Lookman, Osimhen, 20 others for Rwanda, Zimbabwe
content:

title: Amaju Pinnick narrowly loses FIFA Council seat
content:
Nigeria’s candidate, Amaju Melvin Pinnick, very narrowly failed to retain his FIFA Council seat, losing by a single vote at the poll that took place as part of the 14th CAF Extraordinary Congress in Cairo, Egypt on Wednesday.

The former NFF President scored 28 votes, only one short of both Ahmed Yahya of Mauritania and Souleman Hassan Waberi of Djibouti, who each scored 29 votes to make it to the exalted panel.

Morocco’s Fouzi Lekjaa swept 49 votes, with Egypt’s Hany Abou Rida and Niger Republic’s Djibrilla Hima Hamidou netting 35 votes each.

Lekjaa, Rida, Hamidou, Yahya and Waberi will join CAF President Patrice Motsepe, unopposed for a second term, as Africa’s representatives at the FIFA Council, alongside Kanizat Ibrahim from the Comoros Island who collected the women’s seat by scoring 30 votes, as against 13 for former FIFA Council and IOC Member Lydia Nsekera and seven for incumbent Isha Johansen.

Andrew Kamanga (Zambia), Yacine Idriss Diallo (Cote d’Ivoire) and Augustin Senghor (Senegal) polled 19, 18 and 13 votes respectively, while Benin Republic’s Mathurin De Chacus withdrew just before the vote.

In the CAF Executive Committee elections, Alfred Randriamanampisoa (Madagascar) withdrew before the vote, leaving Elvis Chetty (Seychelles), Sobha Mohamed Ally Samir (Mauritius) and Feizal Ismael Sidat (Mozambique) to contest for two COSAFA seats. In the event, Sobha Samir and Feizal Sidat were successful.

Unopposed, as the CAF President, were Wallace Karia (CECAFA, Tanzania), Samuel Eto’o (UNIFFAC, Cameroon), Mustapha Ishola Raji (WAFU A, Liberia), Kurt Edwin-Simeon Okraku (WAFU B, Ghana), Sadhi Walid (UNAF) and Bestine Kazadi Ditabala (Female Seat, DR Congo).

FIFA Council Seats: Patrice Motsepe (South Africa); Fouzi Lekjaa (Morocco); Hany Abou Rida (Egypt); Djibrilla ‘Pele’ Hima Hamidou (Niger Republic); Ahmed Yahya (Mauritania), Souleman Hassan Waberi (Djibouti).

Female Seat: Kanizat Ibrahim (Comoros)

CAF Exco Seats: Samuel Eto’o (UNIFFAC); Wallace Karia (CECAFA); Sadhi Walid (UNAF); Mustapha Ishola Raji (WAFU A); Kurt Edwin-Simeon Okraku (WAFU B); Sobha Mohamed Ally Samir and Feizal Ismael Sidat (COSAFA)

Female Seat: Bestine Kazadi Ditabala (DR Congo).

title: Morocco 2025: Flamingos intensify training as South Africa’s Bantwana land in Lagos
content:
The delegation of South Africa’s U17 girls, Bantwana, is scheduled to arrive in Lagos on Wednesday evening, ahead of Saturday’s FIFA U17 Women’s World Cup second round, second leg qualifying match against Nigeria’s Flamingos.

A brace by Harmony Chidi, which followed Shakirat Moshood’s goal, steered Nigeria to a 3-1 win over their hosts in Pretoria on Saturday, but the Bantwana have sounded a big warning that they will not be in Ikenne to lie down and be slaughtered.

Team captain Katleho Malebana, whose goal early in the second half raised the hopes of the Bantwana, before Chidi’s second and Nigeria’s third, has assured that the South Africans will contest every blade of the grass with their hosts at the Remo Stars Stadium on Saturday.

Saturday’s encounter will kick off at 4pm, with Senegalese match officials in charge. CAF has appointed Aida Sy to serve as referee, while her compatriots Ndeye Aissa Ndiaye, Ndeye Sarr Ndiaye and Fatoumata Sall Toure will be in the roles of assistant 1, assistant 2 and fourth official respectively.

Ghanaian Naa Odofoley Nortey will be the commissioner while Agar Mezing from Cameroon will be the referee assessor.

The winner on aggregate will progress to the final round of the qualification series, with this year’s FIFA U17 Women’s World Cup taking place in Morocco, 17 October – 8 November. Africa will present 5 teams (including host nation Morocco) at the finals, which has been expanded to a 24-nation championship.

The Flamingos have intensified their preparation with training sessions at the Remo Stars Institute, Ikenne-Remo ahead of Saturday’s encounter.

title: NNPCL begin fresh negotiations with the Dangote Petroleum Refinery over Naira-for-crude contract
content:
As the initial deal between Nigerian National Petroleum Company Limited (NNPCL) and Dangote Petroleum Refinery expiration ends on March 31, 2025, the NNPCL has initiated fresh renewal negotiations for the continuation of naira-for-crude agreement.

Recall that on October 1, 2024, the government commenced the sales of crude oil in naira to local refineries to improve supply, save the country millions of dollars in petroleum product imports, and ultimately reduce the pump prices of refined products.

The fresh negotiations was disclosed in a statement on Monday by the NNPCL Chief Corporate Communications Officer, Olufemi Soneye, in response to claims that the government-owned oil company had suspended the naira-for-crude deal until 2030, as it has forward-sold all its crude oil.

“NNPC Limited has noted recent reports circulating on social media regarding the alleged unilateral termination of the crude oil sales agreement in naira between NNPC and Dangote Refinery.

“To clarify, the contract for the sale of crude oil in naira was structured as a six-month agreement, subject to availability, and expires at the end of March 2025. Discussions are currently ongoing towards emplacing a new contract.

“Under this arrangement, NNPC has made over 48 million barrels of crude oil available to Dangote Refinery since October 2024. In aggregate, NNPC has made over 84 million barrels of crude oil available to the refinery since its commencement of operations in 2023.”

“We are commitment to supplying crude oil for local refining based on mutually agreed terms and conditions,” the statement read.

On his part, the Chairman of the Technical Sub-Committee on the naira-for-crude deal, Zacch Adedeji, stated that there is substantial evidence supporting the policy as the correct approach and affirmed that it will continue to contribute positively to the nation’s economy.

“The policy framework enabling the sale of crude oil in naira for domestic refining remains in force. The initiative was designed to ensure supply stability and optimize the utilisation of local refining capacity. There has been no decision at the policy level to discontinue this approach, nor is it being considered. After implementing the policy for some months, evidence abounds that it is the right way to go, and it will continue to help the economy.

“The framework for domestic crude transactions is designed to promote a competitive and efficient pricing environment.

“The engagement process for crude oil supply to domestic refineries therefore remains in place by structured agreements, balancing factors such as availability, demand, and market conditions. There is no exclusion of local refineries from access to domestic crude oil. The Nigerian Upstream Petroleum Regulatory Commission is actively ensuring compliance with the Domestic Crude Oil Obligations provisions of the Petroleum Industry Act.

“We remain committed to ensuring the efficient execution of this initiative in line with its core objectives – enhancing local refining, reducing foreign exchange exposure, and stabilising the domestic fuel supply,” he stated.

title: Tinubu inaugurates youth confab committee to address brain drain
content:
President Bola Tinubu in a statement on Monday while inaugurating the 44 Implementation Committee for the National Youth Conference at the State House, Abuja, has assured Nigerians that his administration’s economic reforms will encourage professionals who left the country in search of better opportunities to return.

The Monday’s inauguration comes five months after Tinubu, in his last Independence Day broadcast, announced plans for a 30-day national youth confab to address critical issues facing the country’s youths.

The implementation process for the youth conference will include virtual consultations, calls for memoranda, regional town hall meetings, and a final congress in Abuja.

The Special Adviser to the President on Information and Strategy, Bayo Onanuga, revealed details of the meeting in a statement he signed Monday titled ‘Nigerian Professionals Will Return As Economy Improves, President Tinubu Assures at Inauguration of National Youth Confab Planning Committee.’

“When you listen to most professionals leaving Nigeria, there’s a cause. If you grow prosperity back home and empower people, they will not bother leaving. They will stay home.

“I want to reassure you that you are the hope of this country, and everything hangs on you.

“Every decision that I have taken is about you. It’s about the future. When we removed the fuel subsidy, it was because we wanted to protect your future.

“We have cleared the path for you to have a great future.

“This is your opportunity to develop the nation and make it prosperous. You are the heartbeat of our nation, and I hope you take this responsibility seriously.

“Just look me in the face and tell me whatever you think is wrong and the way forward.

“Be frank. We will implement your suggestions so long as they are for the country’s prosperity,” he stated.

“When we started, it looked so foggy, dicey, and hopeless. We worked hard, and it was like drawing water out of a dry well.

“But today, the economy has turned the corner; prices are falling, confidence in our economy is improving, investors are looking this way, and technology is advancing,” he added. 

The Minister of Youth Development, Ayodele Olawande, commended the President for prioritising youth inclusion and creating platforms for engagement.

Mr Olubunmi Olusanya, Permanent Secretary of the Ministry of Youth Development will be chairman of the committee, other members are Senate Chairman on Niger Delta Development Commission, Asuquo Ekpeyong, Dr Linus Okorie, Dr Garba Aliyu, Babatunde Adeleke, Francis Sani, Azeezat Yishawu, Sara-Igbe Sukubo, Hauwa Ibrahim, Zara Goni, Oladele Nihi, Dare Ojepe, Uchechukwu George Egbe, among others.

title: Tops English Premiership Clubs Competing For Ademola Lookman
content:
Super Eagles striker, Ademola Lookman is reported to have capture the attention of big Premier cup, with the like of Chelsea and Arsenal showing interest in him.

The Gunners are particularly interested in the 27-year-old, who gained recognition last year for his impressive performances in the Europa League, earning a nomination for the Ballon d’Or.

According to TEAMtalk, both Chelsea and Arsenal have placed Lookman on their shortlist as a possible option for the summer transfer window, although he is not their primary target.

Sources close to Chelsea indicate that Lookman is on the list of potential signings, but a move is considered unlikely as his age and wages are putting into consideration.

On the other hand, Arsenal manager Mikel Arteta has specifically requested the club to sign a proven striker who can help propel the team toward the Premier League title.

title: Super Eagles Open Camp Ahead of Tough Challenge, As Chelle Releases Final Squad This Week
content:
Super Eagles of Nigeria expected to have its camp open for the two FIFA World Cup qualifying games against Rwanda and Zimbabwe on Sunday, 16th March 2025 in Kigali, Rwanda ahead of their World Cup qualifier campaign on 21st March against Rwanda before hosting Zimbabwe four days later at the Godswill Akpabio Stadium in Uyo at 5:00 pm. The two games are must-win for the 2013 African champions.

The Super Eagles are set to face Rwanda and Zimbabwe in match-days 5 and 6 of the qualifiers, with both games being crucial to reviving their fading hopes.

Nigeria's Super Eagles captain, Ahmed Musa, acknowledged the team's challenging position ahead of the next round of World Cup qualifiers, as he emphasized the significance of the upcoming clashes, calling it a potential turning point.

"The most important game is against Rwanda. If we can secure three points from that match, it could change everything for us. But this isn’t just about the Super Eagles—we need the support of every Nigerian.

"We believe in ourselves and our ability to qualify. The Super Eagles cannot afford to miss the 2026 World Cup.

"It would be a huge disaster for Nigerian football if our players are not at the World Cup,”he stated.

Meanwhile, the Head Coach, Eric Chelle, will be expected to release the final squad this week, after the provisional 39-man squad released last week that will execute the matches against Rwanda and Zimbabwe. 

Super Eagles  are sitting fifth on the log with three points from four matches.

title: Gov Sim Fubara Invites Hon. Martins Amaewhule and others Assembly Members After 48-hour ultimatum
content:
Rivers State Governor, Governor Sim Fubara has sent a letter to the Speaker of the Rivers State House of Assembly, Hon. Martins Amaewhule, for a meeting on Monday, March 10, 2025, follows the governor’s receipt of the Supreme Court’s judgment. set for the presentation of the budget.

The invitation which was conveyed in a letter signed by the Secretary to the State Government, Tammy Danagogo, on Sunday is set to discuss:

1. Provision of a befitting space for the Assembly's sittings;

2. Payment of all outstanding remuneration or allowances of the Honourable members;

3. Presentation of Budget and sundry matters;

4. Any other matter(s), as may be necessary, to chart the way forward in the best interest of the State.

The governor expressed his anticipation of the Assembly members’ attendance, stating that the discussion aims to “chart the way forward in the interest of the good people of Rivers State.”

The state Assembly had issued a 48-hour ultimatum to the governor to present the 2025 budget after the Supreme Court judgment.

title: 13th ECOWAS Wrestling Tournament Open In Abuja As Nigeria Restates Commitment To African Unity
content:
The wait is finally over as the highly anticipated 13th ECOWAS African Traditional Wrestling Tournamen Open on Thursday in Abuja.

Nigeria as the host country restated commitment to building African unity through sports

The Chairman, National Sports Commission, Mallam Shehu Dikko at the opening ceremony reiterated the nation's commitment towards unity and economic advancement of West Africa deploying sports as a tool. The NSC Chairman made this commitment in his opening speech at the 13th ECOWAS African Wrestling Tournament at the Velodrome MKO Abiola National Stadium Abuja.

His words, "We are particularly honoured that this prestigious event is taking place at a time when the leadership of ECOWAS is being steered by His Excellency, President Bola Ahmed Tinubu GCFR, the Chairman of the Authority of ECOWAS Heads of State and Government. Under his visionary guidance, ECOWAS continues to champion unity, economic development and the advancement of sports as a tool for peace and regional cohesion. 

"This tournament is a testament to our collective commitment to promoting cultural ties and strengthening the bonds that unite us as West Africans, and indeed proud Africans."

He highlighted the Commission's youth empowerment drive through sports.

"Nigeria is proud to host this prestigious event, reaffirming our commitment to the promotion and development of traditional sports. The National Sports Commission remains dedicated to harnessing sports as a vehicle for youth empowerment, regional integration and economic growth. Through events like this, we provide a platform for young athletes to showcase their talent, create wealth by earning a living through sports, build camaraderie and inspire future generations", he added. 

In his view, such tournaments would strengthen the RHINSE programme of the Commission.

He continued, "This is in line with the Federal Government of Nigeria's Renewed Hope Initiative for Nigeria's Sports Economy (RHINSE) framework, a comprehensive strategy aimed at resetting, refocusing and relaunching Nigeria's sports ecosystem, by developing sports infrastructure enhancing sports development, promotion of domestic competitions and improving the economic contribution of sports to the nation."

Mallam Dikko enjoined the participating nations to look beyond the medals on showcase at the tournament. 

"To our esteemed wrestlers, I urge you to compete with passion, fairness and respect for one another. Remember, beyond the medals and trophies, this tournament represents unity, friendship and the enduring power of sport to bring people together", he concluded. 

Earlier in his statement, Director -General of NSC Hon. Bukola Olopade echoed the nation's resolve to host a very memorable edition of the tournament.

"We are committed to hosting a world-class tournament where all our ECOWAS brothers will compete favourably and go back with lasting memories of their time in Nigeria. I want everyone from the different ECOWAS nations to feel free and savour our unique Nigeria hospitality as we enjoy days of this prestigious tournament", he said.

In her remark, Commissioner for Human Development and Social Affairs ECOWAS Commission Prof. Fatou Sow Sarr represented by Amb. Francis Chuks Njoaguani expressed appreciation to President Bola Ahmed Tinubu for graciously accepting to host the tournament in Nigeria for the first time. In her opinion, the tournament will strengthen the unity in the sub-region.

title: $1.4m proceeds linked to Emefiele forfeited by Court
content:
On Thursday, Justice Ayokunle Faji, of the Federal High Court sitting in Lagos, in his ruling has ordered the final forfeiture of $1.4m alleged fraud proceeds linked to former Governor of the Central Bank of Nigeria, Godwin Emefiele, as he held that the funds were proven to be proceeds of unlawful activities and must be forfeited to the Federal Government.

Justice Faji had initially granted an interim forfeiture order on May 30, 2024, before issuing the final ruling on Thursday.

An affidavit deposed by EFCC investigator David Jayeoba detailed how intelligence reports led to the discovery of the concealed funds.

The investigation allegedly exposed a scheme involving Emefiele and his associates, including Donatone Limited’s directors, Uzeobo Anthony and Adebanjo Olurotimi, who were accused of disguising illicit proceeds.

The EFCC claimed that between 2021 and 2022, amid Nigeria’s forex scarcity, Emefiele and his associates extorted businesses seeking foreign exchange approvals, collecting bribes.

One such company, identified as NP, reportedly deposited $26,552,000 into Donatone Limited’s account at Titan Trust Bank.

Before now, on February 21, 2025, Justice Yellim Bogoro of the Federal High Court ordered the final forfeiture of $4.7m, N830m, and multiple properties linked to Emefiele.

The affected properties include 94 units of an 11-floor building under construction at 2 Otunba Elegushi 2nd Avenue, Ikoyi, Lagos; AM Plaza, an 11-floor office space on Otunba Adedoyin Crescent, Lekki Peninsula Scheme 1, Lagos; and Imore Industrial Park 1, located on Esa Street, Imoore Land, Amuwo Odofin LGA, Lagos. Others are Mitrewood and Tatler Warehouse (Furniture Plant at Bogije) near Elemoro, Owolomi Village, Ibeju-Lekki LGA, Lagos, as well as two properties purchased from Chevron Nigeria in Lakes Estate, Lekki, Lagos.

Additional properties affected by the order include a plot at Lekki Foreshore Estate Scheme, Foreshore Estate, Eti-Osa LGA; an estate at 100 Cottonwood Coppel Texas Drive, Coppel, Texas, owned by Lipam Investment Services; land at 1 Bunmi Owulude Street, Lekki Phase 1, Lagos; and a property at 8 Bayo Kuku Road, Ikoyi, Lagos.

This comes after a previous forfeiture order on November 1, 2024, when Justice Deinde Dipeolu of the Federal High Court ordered the permanent forfeiture of $2.045m, seven prime landed properties, and share certificates linked to Emefiele.

Justice Dipeolu ruled that the funds and share certificates of Queensdorf Global Fund Limited Trust be permanently forfeited to the Federal Government.

title: N80.2bn Fraud: Yahaya Bello paid $2,452,615.68 till children graduation and Advance future enrolment
content:
In the ongoing of N80.2bn fraud charge filed by the EFCC against the former Governor of Kogi State, Yahaya Bello, an auditor of the American International School, Abuja, Nicholas Ojehomon, on Wednesday has told the Federal High Court sitting in Abuja that the former Governor paid a total of $1,606,763.68 in tuition fees for his children, including an advance payment of $845,852 for his young children to be enrolled in the school in the future.

He disclosed this while testifying as a prosecution witness for the Economic and Financial Crimes Commission. He confirmed that the payments covered Bello’s children’s tuition until graduation which was paid in two tranches, with one part serving as an advance for future tuition fees.

“Mr. Ali Bello contacted the American International School, Abuja, on Friday, August 13, requesting to pay the Bello children’s school fees until they graduate. The school management accepted his offer.
