Mikel said Aina has improved tremendously since he left Chelsea.

title: Unpatriotic: Food Diversion By Farmers Responsible For The High Cost - Governors Abdulrahman
content:
Mallam Abdulrahman Abdulrazak, the Governor of Kwara State and the chairman of Nigeria Governors Forum during a New Year visit by Vice President Kashim Shettima and members of the Nigeria Governors Forum (NGF) to president Tinubu at his Ikoyi residence in Lagos on Wednesday stated that diversion of farm produce to foreign countries for maximum gain by farmers because of naira devaluation are responsible for high cost of food items and not the policies anymore.

According to him food inflation would have drop if the farmers are patriotic enough to put Nigeria first before excess personal gain.

"The policies are working. In agriculture, I was in Jigawa, the complaint in Jigawa was that there was a bumper harvest, but because of the strength of our currency, traders exported the harvest.

"So, most of us are encouraging ourselves to buy bumper stocks into our silos, store them for the rainy day. So, in terms of agriculture, the policy is working. We'll continue to deepen that and ensure we are 100% sustained in food security and feed the whole of West Africa," he said.

The governor urged the President to visit various states to see the ongoing transformations and progress firsthand, as he assured the President of the steadfast support of the governors, particularly in contributing to local security architecture to further enhance the nation's security.

"I must confess that I have not done two years in this administration, but I've done more projects in two years than in the four years of my first term.

"We are getting more funding due to the restructuring of the economy. Yes, there is inflation, but we are overriding it," the governor said.

Reacting to President Tinubu as ThisDay's Man of the Year, he described the decision as a significant endorsement of the administration's policies, while notes that the acknowledgement from a media outlet known for critical media coverage during the campaign reflects the tangible progress made under President Tinubu's leadership.

title: I shouldn't be In Battle With You Over LG autonomy - Tinubu Tells Govs
content:
During a New Year homage by Vice President Kashim Shettima and members of the Nigeria Governors Forum (NGF) on Wednesday at his Ikoyi residence in Lagos, the President emphasised the critical role of state governors in driving Nigeria's development and prosperity while expressed his gratitude for their support and collaboration, saying their leadership at the subnational level is central to achieving food security, economic prosperity and rapid national growth.

He highlighting key areas requiring joint effort for the nation's progress while reiterating that his administration is in no battle with state governors over the controversial local government autonomy.

President Tinubu called for stronger collaboration between the federal and state governments to address pressing challenges, including local government autonomy, agricultural productivity, and currency stability.

Expressing his commitment to local government development and autonomy, the President stressed its importance for grassroots development and dispelled rumours of disagreement with the governors.

Tinubu’s Special Adviser on Information and Strategy, Bayo Onanuga, revealed the discussions in a statement he signed Wednesday titled, ‘President Tinubu to Governors: You are the most important link to Nigeria’s development and prosperity.’

"You are the most important link to Nigeria's prosperity and development. The Federal Government accounts for about 30 to 35 per cent of the allocated revenue; the rest comes to you. The agricultural value chain depends on you. You own the land, and the job is in your hands.

"We will not fight within us. I will drive the change. You control your local governments. You can restore hope by effectively fulfilling what the people expect at the grassroots level.

"There were gossips that we had disagreements on local government autonomy. No. Just drive development at the local government. Nobody wants to take them away from you, but we need collaboration. Let's do it together and ensure Nigeria is better off for it.

"We have to work harder, grow more, and ensure the situation of our currency improves. Nigeria will see prosperity, but it requires consistent effort from all of us.

"There is no state we cannot visit and be proud of its development. We have better allocations now. Let me take the abuse; you take the privileges. Together, we will build a nation we are all proud of.

"I am glad I asked for this job, and Nigerians gave me the mandate. We'll be on this voyage together. I thank all of you for where we are today and where we are heading,”the president said in the statement.

The President also announced that he will be visiting Enugu State on January 4 as part of his planned visits to some states of the federation, while welcomed his declaration by ThisDAY newspaper as Man Of The Year. "What they considered a failure initially, but  is now a success," he said has he commended the newspaper for recognition

The governors on the New Year visit were Abba Yusuf (Kano), Sheriff Oborevwori (Delta), AbdulRahman AbdulRazaq (Kwara); Babajide Sanwo-Olu (Lagos), Siminalayi Fubara (Rivers) and Lucky Aiyedatiwa (Ondo), Governors Babagana Zulum (Borno), Monday Okpebholo (Edo); Biodun Oyebanji (Ekiti), Peter Mbah (Enugu), Abdullahi Sule (Nasarawa), Hope Uzodimma (Imo) and Usman Ododo (Kogi).

In July 2024, the Supreme Court delivered a landmark judgment affirming the fiscal autonomy of local governments nationwide.

The apex court ruled that it is unconstitutional for state governors to hold funds allocated for local government administrations.

Therefore, local governments must receive direct allocations from the Federation Account, without interference by state governments.

title: 2025: President, Senate President, Speaker  Resolved To Take Nigeria To Promised Land At A Meeting
content:
President Bola Tinubu said his administration is encouraged by the National Assembly's support over the last 19 months and is determined to take Nigeria to the Promised Land as it was disclosed by Bayo Onanuga, president spoke person.

The President spoke Wednesday while receiving Vice President Kashim Shettima, the leadership of the National Assembly, and former principal officers of the National Assembly at his Oyinkan Abayomi Drive residence in Ikoyi, Lagos.

The New Year homage, led by Senate President Godswill Akpabio, preceded a similar visit by members of the Nigeria Governors Forum (NGF).

"Nigerians are the heart of everything we are doing. We have come to serve. You have made my day by coming on this visit. Happy New Year. May God bless you and our country and give our nation more prosperity.

"The transformative journey we have embarked upon is for all of us. It is for our tomorrow. It is for the future generation. Your commitment will yield that fruit for the babies yet unborn.

"Your commitment to value addition and bringing about the spirit of can do and must do is for all of us together.

"It is for us to build a nation. We have confidence and competence. The enslavers want us to be anything but enslaved people, but we say no. We are determined, we are capable, and we are resolute, and we will be there. We will take Nigeria to that Promised Land with you,'' President Tinubu said at the meeting.

Acknowledging the encouragement from the lawmakers, the President pledged to work harder, embrace intellectual inquisitiveness, and make courageous decisions for national development.

"We have a saying in Yoruba that it is only a courageous dog that will capture the animal in the bush," he added.

Senate President Akpabio commended the President for his courage and commitment to reform and assured him that the National Assembly is firmly behind his administration.

"On this journey of restoration, transformation and rebuilding the nation, you are not alone. The National Assembly is with you and will stand by you," he said.

Akpabio highlighted the positive economic outlook under the Tinubu administration, citing achievements such as over subscription of Nigeria's Eurobond, improvements in ease of doing business, and growing foreign investor confidence.

"We salute our men in uniform and commend you for your bold reforms. Investors remain interested in Nigeria because of your leadership, and we will continue to smile as the benefits materialise," he added.

Speaker of the House of Representatives, Rt. Hon. Tajudeen Abbas commended the President for his respect and support of the National Assembly.

He said many key figures in the administration, including the President, Vice President, Wife of the President, Chief of Staff to the President, Secretary to the Government of the Federation, and several ministers, were all former members of the National Assembly.

''The National Assembly should consider itself lucky, and to God be the glory, Mr President, the National Assembly today is more united than ever.

''The National Assembly is more fulfilled than ever before because there is nothing we have ever knocked on your door to request for the National Assembly that you have not obliged.

''This is historic. This is commendable. We need to thank you for that. I also want to thank you for bringing more succour to the poor.

''Nigerians had more challenges at the beginning of 2023, but as the year ended, more food and prosperity started pouring in. We believe 2025 will be the ultimate year where every Nigerian will be proud of this administration, '' he said.

title: Inflation will drop from %34.6 to 15% this year - Tinubu stated while giving his 2025 speech
content:
President Bola Tinubu in his 2025 speech to Nigerians has assured the citizens that things with be better in the year 2025 as all indicators are pointing to positive and greater economy with an anticipation of reducing inflation from %34.6 to 15%.

Tinubu said: "Fellow Nigerians, as we enter 2025, I wish everyone a happy and prosperous New Year. May you be rich in joy, success, and good health.

"As the new year dawns, it brings many hopes, aspirations, and prospects for better days. By the grace of God, 2025 will be a year of great promise in which we will fulfil our collective hopes.

"Though 2024 posed numerous challenges to our citizens and households, I am confident that the New Year will bring brighter days.

"Economic indicators point to a positive and encouraging outlook for our nation. Fuel prices have gradually decreased, and we recorded foreign trade surpluses in three consecutive quarters. Foreign reserves have risen, and the Naira has strengthened against the US dollar, bringing greater stability.

"The stock market's record growth has generated trillions of naira in wealth, and the surge in foreign investment reflects renewed confidence in our economy. "Nevertheless, the cost of food and essential drugs remained a significant concern for many Nigerian households in 2024.

"In 2025, our government is committed to intensifying efforts to lower these costs by boosting food production and promoting local manufacturing of essential drugs and other medical supplies. We are resolute in our ambition to reduce inflation from its current high of 34.6% to 15%. With diligent work and God's help, we will achieve this goal and provide relief to all our people.

In this new year, my administration will further consolidate and increase access to credit for individuals and critical sectors of the economy to boost national economic output.

"To achieve this, the federal government will establish the National Credit Guarantee Company to expand risk-sharing instruments for financial institutions and enterprises.

"The Company—expected to start operations before the end of the second quarter—is a partnership of government institutions, such as the Bank of Industry, Nigerian Consumer Credit Corporation, the Nigerian Sovereign Investment Agency, and Ministry of Finance Incorporated, the private sector, and multilateral institutions.

"This initiative will strengthen the confidence of the financial system, expand credit access, and support under-served groups such as women and youth. It will drive growth, re-industrialisation, and better living standards for our people.

title: Top 5 List Of Nigerians With Highest Goal Contributors In 2024
content:
As the year 2024 ended, we bring to you Nigerian internationals with the highest goal contributors in the outgoing year.

Nigerian players are making impressive contribution across Europeans countries in their respective clubs as well for the national team. Even though some have it rough at the beginning before found peace and form.

Below are the top five highest Nigerian goals-contributors in 2024

Ademola Lookman (Atalanta – 22 goals and 12 assists)

Ademola Lookman, the current CAF Awards Best Player Men’s, has made an impressive impact in the year in review, emerging as the top Nigerian goal contributor with 22 goals and 12 assists in 42 matches across all competitions (excluding friendlies) for Atalanta.

Lookman kicked off on a noteworthy note in the year 2024 when returned to the pitch on February 25 despite an initial setback, with his first goal against Bologna and first assist against Cagliari shortly after.

His hat-trick in the UEFA Europa League final against Bayer 04 Leverkusen earned Atalanta their first European title.

Second on the log is Cyril Dessers (Rangers – 25 goals and 8 assists)

Cyril Dessers has had a highly productive year with Glasgow Rangers, accumulating 25 goals and eight assists over 54 games.

While he boasts the highest goal tally of all Nigerian strikers on this list, Lookman surpasses him in combined goals and assists. Dessers began his year with an assist against Kilmarnock, quickly following up with his first goal shortly thereafter in the Scottish Cup. His consistency and offensive contributions have made a significant impact on his club.

Third is Victor Osimhen (Napoli/Galatasaray – 21 goals and 4 assists)

Even though Victor Osimhen started his 2024 campaign in February, his form was good enough to finish the year as the second-highest Nigerian goal contributor behind Ademola Lookman.

Osimhen had a dynamic year after his return to club football in February. The 2024 proved to be a challenging season for Osimhen, especially during the tumultuous summer transfer window, but he navigated these challenges effectively to come out triumph.

He started the year with a strong performance against Barcelona in the UEFA Champions League, where he scored for Napoli.

Following a difficult period with Napoli, he transitioned to Galatasaray, where he immediately found form, contributing three assists and scoring twice in a memorable match against Kasimpasa. His closing performance of the year featured another brace to help secure his new team’s top-league position.

Fourth player is Tolu Arokodare (Genk – 20 goals and 4 assists)

Tolu Arokodare opened the year with a goal on February 11 and has maintained strong form ever since, leading the Belgium Pro League scoring chart with 13 goals in just 20 games. His excellent performance has played a crucial role in Genk’s success, as the team currently sits atop the league standings.

While Victor Boniface (Bayer Leverkusen – 13 goals and 2 assists)  came fifth

Despite facing injury challenges at the start of 2024, Victor Boniface has shown promise when fit, contributing 13 goals and two assists in 26 matches for Bayer Leverkusen.

After missing three months due to injury and the AFCON, Boniface made a strong comeback in April, scoring in his return match and continuing to demonstrate his goal-scoring ability until his recent thigh injury sidelined him.

title: Nigeria To Face Libya Again In Qualifier
content:
Former AfroBasket champions and four-time continental silver medalists, Nigeria, will face Libya and two others to compete in the last and final window of AFCON qualifier for the 31st edition of Africa's most prestigious continental men's basketball championship, ‘FIBA Men's AfroBasket 2025’

The tournament will take place in Luanda, the Angolan capital between the 12th and 24th of August, 2025, for the fourth time after they hosted the event in 1989, 1999 and 2007.

After the draws, the Nigeria Basketball Federation (NBBF) stated that building up for the last and crucial qualifying window for the Championship, its has started linking up with players they hope to invite, while some had been formally invited to be part of D'Tigers who are expected roar and secure one of the two tickets still up for grab from Group B.

The NBBF President, Engineer Musa Kida, confrim that the team will be a mixture of home based players and players plying their trade outside the shores of Nigeria.

On his part, the NBBF Vice President who also doubles as Technical Director, Babatunde Ogunade, said: “We can only work with the players available during this window, but more importantly the National Sports Commission (NSC), should provide the much needed funds on time.”

Nigeria needs to win at least two of the three games with hope Uganda bottles it chances. Cape Verde currently on 6 points are certain to reach the finals next year even with three defeats in this Window.

Host Lybia with 5 points will land in Angola with two more wins while Nigeria's voyage to Luanda will end if Uganda picks two wins in this Qualifying Window.

title: Asari-Dokubo Enthrone As Traditional Rulers In Rivers by Gov Fubara
content:
Former Niger Delta militant leader, Alhaji Mujahid Asari-Dokubo, and three others has been presented Certificates of Recognition and Staff of Office as a traditional rulers in Rivers State by governor Siminalayi Fubara.

Dokubo-Asari was presented with a certificate and staff of office as the Amanyanabo of Torusarama Piri in Degema local government area of the state, HRM, Winston Odize Alamina Oputibeya XII, as the Amanyanabo of Koniju in Okrika local government area; HRM Eze Noble Friday Uwo as the Eze Igbu-Ehuda (Ahoada) IV in Ahoada-East local hovernment area and HRH Prince Ike Ehie as the Eze Igbu Orilukwoe in Ahoada-East local government area of the state.

While presenting the certificates and staff of office to the four new traditional rulers at Government House, Port Harcourt on Tuesday, Governor Fubara said: “Let me first of all, on behalf of the government, congratulate the four of you. It has not been an easy journey to get to this point. I know a lot of you have been working very hard to ensure the success of this day. Your appointment in terms of this recognition is not for personal aggrandizement, but a call for service, a responsibility to help us protect lives and property in your domains.

“I don’t want you to see this elevation as another platform to create problems in your locality. We have the power to still withdraw the recognition, but I don’t intend to do that. So, I want you to be partners with the government to ensure that we continue to succeed.

“I know that you are all men of integrity. Support the course of governance so that we can all succeed together. It is really a privileged position, and I am very sure that you are going to use it to the best of the interest of your people.”

title: I Falsify Missing Of The N180m NGO Money — VeryDarkMan said as he defend Tinubu
content:
Claims of Controversial social media activist and online police, Martin Otse, widely known as VeryDarkMan has take new turn following the backlash he received for his allege missing of donors ₦180 million money donated to his NGO’s.

Recalls that last week VDM in a viral post stated that a sum of N180m is missing from his NGO as a result of hackers who hacked into the NGO website to made away with the said amount, claiming that one of the suspects has been arrested, and that the current balance of the account now is N20 millions while N160 millions has been diverted.

"For the past few days, I haven't been myself, and it hasn't been easy. The truth is that somebody hacked into the NGO website, and 180 million naira is missing. We have tracked the person, and they've arrested one. The account now has N20 million, but N160 million was diverted. I am on my way to Jos, and hopefully, I will be able to recover all the money back," VDM said in the post.

Fast-forward, he admitted of fabricating the story of ₦180 million allegedly missing from his NGO’s account just to experiment how Nigerians readily believe and spread unverified information on social media.

“Alright, since the ₦180 million naira missing from the NGO account, I have been seeing a lot of comments that I never expected, but I really want to thank God because everything I have done on this social media I did it because this is who I am. I did not do it to seek public validation.

“I saw all those comments, and I asked myself, what is my offence? All I do on social media is to advocate, help people collect back their money, and create awareness so people won’t be scammed. Most times, I even put my money into these efforts, sometimes borrowing, because I want Nigeria to be a place where people have a voice.

“Some people were even insulting my mother, calling her a thief.

“You know 80% of the people that use social media are stupid, right? This whole thing that happened is a clear opportunity to show you. I deliberately did it to show you people that you are stupid.

“We are in a country where anything said on social media, nobody bothers to check, nobody bothers to investigate. Everybody starts sharing, they start running away with it. They don’t even waste time to listen; boom! They just want to comment: ‘₦180 million is missing, VeryDarkMan is a thief.’ Nobody sat down to analyze, ‘Wait, the VeryDarkMan we know—if ₦180 million is missing from his NGO account, will he be going to Jos instead of Abuja where the police, EFCC, and cybercrime headquarters are located?’ What is he going to do in Jos?.

“The whole media has been spoilt, has been ruined. That’s why one man from Niger came recently and said the French government gave Tinubu money to open a military base in the North East. Nobody sat down to ask, ‘Did this man present any evidence? Did he show a video or proof of the foundation being laid?’ He just said it, and boom, that’s it!.

“80% of you on social media are very, very stupid,” he said.

title: N2.7tn Misappropriated By CBN – Auditor General Of Federation
content:
The Federal Government in its consolidated financial statement for the year ended December 31, 2021, submitted to the National Assembly by the Auditor-General, Shaakaar Chira, with reference number AuGF/AR.2021/01, dated July 31, 2024 has accused the Central Bank of Nigeria for misappropriated N2.73tn in interest payments from Ways and Means advances

Chira, citing irregularities in the management of the facility. Ways and Means facility is a temporary loan mechanism provided by the CBN to the government to finance budget deficits.

The report stated that the CBN retained interest charges amounting to N2.73tn and use it for its sole benefit rather than returning them to the Consolidated Revenue Fund which violated Section 80(2) of the 1999 Constitution of Federal Republic of Nigeria (as amended) that said no funds shall be withdrawn from the CRF without approval by an appropriation act or supplementary act. Its also go against the paragraph 710 of the Financial Regulations of 2009 that bars overdrafts and mandates that any interest incurred must be refunded.

“The CRF negative balance of (N17,105,111,709,523.00) as at 31st December 2021 included actual Ways and Means advance of N4.4 trillion taken by Government and interest charged on it for the sole use of CBN as though the Ways and Means a loan from CBN funds or from any syndicated group of lenders.

“The interest charged on Ways and Means by CBN was misappropriated by CBN for its sole use whereas the Actual Ways and Means was not a facility from its funds or balance sheet, nor was it a syndicated facility from a group of local and foreign lenders.

“CBN must therefore refund to the Federal Government of Nigeria the interest of N2.73 trillion it cornered for its sole use as of 31st December 2021 unless the Federal Government provided evidence of proper approvals and documentation for the transactions.

“The interest charges should not be securitised, unlike other components of the overdraft being handled by the Debt Management Office.

“Unauthorised financing of expenditures and avoidable interest payments should not be encourage as its exposed the government to unnecessary fiscal burdens,” the report stated.

title: Lazio Coach - Dele-Bashiru Is Physically Very Effective But...
content:
Aftermath of the final game of 2024 on Sunday between the table leader Atalanta and Lazio which ended 1-1 draw, the coach of the Italian Serie A side Lazio Marco Baroni has heaped praises on the Nigerian International Fisayo Dele-Bashiru while pointed out where he needs to improve to become a top tier player.

Dele-Bashiru was very instrumental in the Lazio midfield and was also star of the game, as he scored the only goal that earned Lazio a valuable point.

Baroni, while commenting on the game and performance of the Nigeria international said, "Dele is improving every day, he played a lot in the Europa League this season and perhaps needs more quality in his passing, but is physically very effective.

“We can often find players between the lines, and this is why a lad like Dele-Bashiru needs a bit more work to fit in with this attitude, as he is perhaps not used to it.”

title: Ademola Lookman Next Move In January Transfer Window
content:
The Nigeria Super Eagle and Atalanta forward, Ademola Lookman who has been in the best form for Gian Piero Gasperini’s side this season scoring 11 goals and six assists in 20 appearances across all competitions for the Serie A leaders has become subject matter for the January transfer window with the like of Premier League giant, Liverpool also interested in him.

Reacting to the development, Tony D’Amico, Atalanta director, says the Nigerian forward won’t be allowed to leave during the January transfer window as he declared that La Dea wants to maintain a full squad until the end of the season.

“Certainly, the January transfer window is a difficult one for all clubs, if there are any opportunities we will go for them but have to maintain the full squad that we currently have at our disposal,” D’Amico told Sky Sport Italia.

On his part, Lookman is more determine and looking beyond the circumstance surrounding his transfer has he promised that 2025 will be a better year for Atalanta.

La Dea currently occupy top spot on the Serie A table, despite 1-1 draw against Lazio in their final game of 2024 on Sunday as they aim to win their first Scudetto.

Atalanta held Lazio to a 1-1 draw in their final game of 2024 on Sunday.

Lookman was named Man of the Match after provided the assist of the only goal for the visitors.

“The club had a fantastic 2024, so we want to continue doing the same thing and the New Year will be better.

 “It was a tough match, the first half was very difficult for us, but we fought and on another day might have won the game.

“We drew, but we didn’t lose, so it’s positive,” he told Sky Sport Italia.

title: CHAN Qualification: NSC Chairman Dikko Rewards Super Eagles B With ₦10 Million
content:
Following Super Eagles B team 3-1 victory over Ghana’s Black Galaxies in Uyo, Akwa Ibom State on Saturday to secured their place in the 8th African Nations Championship (CHAN) scheduled for Tanzania, Kenya and Uganda in February 2025, the Chairman of National Sports Commission (NSC), Mallam Shehu Dikko, has fulfilled his personal donation of ₦10 million to the team.

The pledge was made before the game as revealed by the NSC Director General, Hon. Bukola Olopade, who initially expressed his own intention to personally reward the team for a win before Mallam Dikko show of leadership to take up gesture by himself.

“before the game, I made a personal pledge to reward the team if they emerged victorious. When I shared this with the NSC chairman, Mallam Shehu Dikko, he immediately applauded the idea but insisted that he would make the donation himself as a sign of solidarity and appreciation for the players’ efforts.

“It was a heartfelt moment that truly shows his passion for Nigerian football and the athletes who represent our country. His generosity has further inspired the team, and we are incredibly grateful for his leadership,”Hon. Olopade said.

The game ended 3-1 in favour of the host.Super Eagles B team efforts paid off in the 6th minute via Sadiq Ismail, with another quickfire goals from Nduka Junior and Isaac Saviour to put Nigeria 3-0 ahead under 30 minutes and stay firm in control of the game going into the halftime before Black Galaxies were able to reduce the deficit in the 71st minute through Amakhona Stephen.

The 2025 CHAN tournament which exclusively features players competing in Africa will be co-hosted by Kenya, Uganda, and Tanzania from February 1 to 28.

title: 2025 CHAN: Super Eagles Thrash Ghana To Picks Qualification Ticket
content:
Nigeria's home-based Eagles after massive victory over rival Ghana on Saturday at the Godswill Akpabio Stadium in Uyo, Akwa Ibom State, has qualified for the 2025 Championship of African Nations competition.

The host dominated the game, and their efforts paid off in the 6th minute via Sadiq Ismail, with another quickfire goals from Nduka Junior and Isaac Saviour to put Nigeria 3-0 ahead under 30 minutes and stay firm in control of the game going into the halftime.

The Black Galaxies came back a bit stronger in the second half and they were able to reduce the deficit in the 71st minute through Amakhona Stephen.

The game ended 3-1 in favour of the host and earn them the ticket to the eighth instalment of the competition scheduled for Tanzania, Kenya and Uganda in February 2025, as first leg of the qualification ended goalless draw.

Following the disappointment from the result, Ghana Black Galaxies Head Coach, Mas-Ud Didi Dramani, appeared dejected, admitting Nigeria’s hunger and determination were decisive. While accept Super Eagles B’s superiority over his team  during the post-match press conference when asked about his feelings after the loss.

“Every coach will feel disappointed, but the result remains what it is.

“Nigeria showed much more hunger and did a lot of running. We gave away some key moments in the game, which turned out to be disastrous for us.

“After the first goal, the second can drain the strength and energy of a team because of the manner it was scored — not to mention the third goal. At that point, any team could lose its steam. I think Nigeria showed a lot more hunger to get the win, especially in the first half,” Dramani stated.

The defeat means Ghana will miss both the 2025 CHAN scheduled for Tanzania, Kenya and Uganda and 2025 AFCON in Morocco.

When asked if Ghanaian football is in turmoil, Dramani instead described it as a ‘transitional phase.’

“Every team or country goes through some transitional phase,” he said solemnly. “I think we’re currently in that phase.

“These are lessons learned in good faith. We don’t like failure, but sometimes failure brings a moment to reflect and then bounce back in the right way.”

Nigeria and Ghana, two West African football powerhouses, often meet in the qualifying stages of major African competitions, with one inevitably being eliminated.

When asked if this arrangement deprives the sub-region of quality representation or denies the continent one of its best teams in major tournaments, Dramani urged CAF to re-evaluate its competition formats.

“I think that’s one of the key issues CAF has to address. It’s important for the body to critically examine this and come up with a format that ensures the best for the continent,” Dramani concluded.

title: Osimhen Revealed Final Decision On His Next Move
content:
The Super Eagle and Galatasaray in-form forward Victor Osimhen has clear the air regarding his next move.

Osimhen who is on loan to Galatasaray from Napoli at the beginning of the season continue to be the in news for possible move away from his club due to his brilliant performance so far with interest from top flight clubs

In latest development, Osimhen confirmed his intention to remain at Galatasaray at least until the end of the current season, putting to rest any speculation about a possible departure in the January transfer window.

Recall, just last week, Sacha Tavolieri claimed that Manchester United have made contact with Osimhen representative to solve Ruben Amorim puzzle of looking for a perfect striker.

RMC Sport also reported that PSG has reached out to Osimhen, who is aware of their interest but remains happy in Turkey, where he’s been warmly received.

Galatasaray's manager, Okan Buruk, reiterated in a recent interview that both the player and the club share the objective of him to remain in the club at least until the end of the current season.

Osimhen outstanding performances have played a significant role in keeping the team at the top of the league, leading the Turkish league's top-scorers chart with 12 goals in 15 games.

However, Buruk assured that the attacker is completely satisfied in Istanbul.

"He is happy here and wants to stay with us until the end of the season," the coach emphasized.

Buruk also highlighted the importance of keeping the Nigerian focused on his performance rather than on any future negotiations.

According to the MundoDeportivo, while Galatasaray hopes to acquire him permanently, the coach insisted that the priority is to create a suitable environment for the striker to continue to excel.

The 25-year-old joined Galatasaray on loan in September with a break-up in the contract which allows him to leave the Turkish Super Lig champions in January transfer window on a release clause believed to be around €75 million, potentially dropping to €70 million next summer.

title: How to find Part Time Jobs for Students in Dubai - Courtesy Of Bright Scholarship
content:
Dubai, known for its luxurious lifestyle and booming economy, is not just a destination for tourists and professionals but also a hub for students seeking part-time work opportunities. For many students, working part-time is essential to support their living expenses, gain practical experience, and build a network in a competitive job market. This guide explores the landscape of part time jobs for students in Dubai, highlighting the best options, application strategies, and tips for balancing work and studies.

Why Work Part-Time in Dubai?

Financial Support: Dubai’s cost of living can be high, and part-time jobs help students manage expenses like rent, food, and transportation.

Experience Building: Employers value real-world experience. Part-time jobs can boost your resume, making you stand out in the job market.

Networking Opportunities: Dubai is a global business hub, offering students exposure to diverse industries and professionals.

Flexible Work Laws for Students: Recent changes in Dubai’s labor laws have made it easier for students to work legally, especially under student visas with part-time work permits.

Top Part Time Jobs for Students in Dubai

1. Retail Sales Associate

· Where: Malls, boutique stores, and electronics outlets.

· Job Description: Assisting customers, managing inventory, and processing transactions.

· Skills Required: Communication, customer service, and basic knowledge of sales software.

· Pay Scale: AED 30–50/hour.

2. Freelance Content Writer or Social Media Manager

· Where: Digital marketing agencies, startups, or freelance platforms like Upwork and Fiverr.

· Job Description: Creating content, managing social media accounts, and planning marketing campaigns.

· Skills Required: Writing, editing, and familiarity with platforms like Instagram and LinkedIn.

· Pay Scale: AED 50–100/hour, depending on experience.

3. Tutoring

· Where: Private households, tutoring centers, or online platforms like Wyzant and Preply.

· Job Description: Teaching subjects like math, science, or language skills to school children or other students.

· Skills Required: Expertise in the subject area and good communication.

· Pay Scale: AED 75–150/hour.

4. Food Delivery Rider

· Where: Apps like Deliveroo, Talabat, and Zomato.

· Job Description: Delivering food from restaurants to customers.

· Skills Required: Valid UAE driver’s license and navigation skills.

· Pay Scale: AED 15–30 per delivery plus tips.

5. Event Assistant

· Where: Event management companies, trade expos, and concerts.

· Job Description: Helping organize and execute events, including guest assistance, setup, and logistics.

· Skills Required: Organizational skills, adaptability, and energy.

· Pay Scale: AED 40–70/hour.

6. Barista or Waiter/Waitress

· Where: Coffee shops and restaurants like Starbucks, Costa, or local cafes.

· Job Description: Taking orders, serving customers, and managing basic cafe operations.

· Skills Required: Customer service and time management.

· Pay Scale: AED 30–60/hour.

7. Data Entry Specialist

· Where: Offices, temporary project setups, or remote roles.

· Job Description: Inputting and organizing data into systems.

· Skills Required: Attention to detail and proficiency in Microsoft Excel or other database tools.

· Pay Scale: AED 20–40/hour.

How to Find Part-Time Jobs in Dubai

1. Online Job Portals

Platforms like Bayt, LinkedIn, and Dubizzle are excellent for finding part-time positions tailored to students.

2. University Career Centers

Many universities in Dubai collaborate with businesses to offer exclusive part-time opportunities to students.

3. Networking

Networking events and meetups in Dubai are great for connecting with professionals and finding job openings.

4. Freelance Platforms

Websites like Upwork and Fiverr allow students to find flexible freelance jobs that can be done from home.

Legal Considerations for Students Working Part-Time in Dubai

1. Work Permit Requirements: Students on a UAE visa must obtain a part-time work permit from the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation (MOHRE).

2. Employer Restrictions: Only companies within free zones like Dubai Knowledge Park and Dubai Internet City can hire part-time student workers.

3. Hourly Limitations: Students can work a maximum of 20 hours per week to ensure they balance work and academic responsibilities.

Balancing Work and Studies

Working part-time while studying can be challenging but manageable with the right approach:

· Set Priorities: Focus on your studies first, as they are your primary objective.

· Choose Flexible Jobs: Look for roles with adjustable schedules, like freelancing or weekend shifts.

· Plan Your Time: Use tools like Google Calendar to organize your schedule efficiently.

· Communicate with Employers: Inform your employer about your class timings and exam schedules to avoid conflicts.

Essential Skills to Succeed in Part-Time Jobs

Employers in Dubai value the following skills for part-time roles:

1. Communication: Essential for customer-facing roles like retail and hospitality.

2. Time Management: Balancing work, studies, and personal life requires efficient time management.

3. Adaptability: Dubai’s dynamic work environment requires you to be flexible and quick to learn.

4. Technical Proficiency: Familiarity with tools like Excel, WordPress, or graphic design software can be an advantage.

Future Opportunities from Part-Time Jobs

Part-time jobs can open the door to full-time roles. For example:

· Retail Jobs: Often lead to supervisory or managerial positions.

· Freelancing: Helps build a portfolio, which can attract high-paying clients.

· Tutoring: Builds teaching experience, a stepping stone for academic or training careers.

title: Martin Vincent Otse know as Verydarkman loss N180m donors money to hackers
content:
Popular online police and social media activist, Martin Vincent Otse know as VDM has made revelation on how N180 millions donors money was loss to hackers.

He stated that a sum of N180m is missing from his NGO as a result of hackers who hacked into the NGO website to made away with the said amount. Though he said one of the suspects has been arrested, and that the current balance of the account now is N20 millions while N60 millions has been diverted.

"For the past few days, I haven't been myself, and it hasn't been easy. The truth is that somebody hacked into the NGO website, and 180 million naira is missing. I am on my way to Jos, and hopefully, I will be able to recover all the money back," VDM said.

title: Fulham Stun Chelsea At Stamford Bridge AS Nottingham Forest Move To 3rd Spot
content:
Fulham came from behind to beat neighbours Chelsea 2-1 after a 95th minute goal from substitute Rodrigo Muniz which gave the visitors all three points in the Premier League on Thursday.

Chelsea first took the lead in the 16 minutes when Cole Palmer danced past two defenders and slid the ball through Issa Diop’s legs into the bottom corner to score a classy goal.

But the second half determination of Fulham’s paid off in the 82nd minute when Harry Wilson headed home from close range for the club’s first goal at Stamford Bridge since 2011, before a roundup second goal from Rodrigo Muniz in the 95th minute to clinched the three points.

The win was also Fulham’s first win at Stamford Bridge since 1979.

In another game, Nottingham Forest moved up to third spot in the Premier League table after a narrow win over Tottenham with 1-0

Goal from the in-form winger Anthony Elanga sealed the three point needed.

The win is Forest fourth successive win in the top flight for the first time since 1995, and also Nuno Espirito Santo first win over Tottenham – who had ex-Forest defender Djed Spence sent off in injury time – since being sacked by them three years ago.

Nuno lasted just four months in North London and, when he was dismissed in November 2021, his stock in England had fallen following a stale end to his four years at Wolves.

With victory, Forest have more points than during last season’s successful survival fight in half the games to underline the rapid progress made under Nuno, who has restored his reputation.

Chelsea’s still in second place on a 35 points, seven points off the table leaders Liverpool which have one game more at hand. While Nottingham Forest sit at third place with 34 point.

title: Atiku Berate CDS Stance On Sokoto Airstrike
content:
Former Vice President Atiku Abubakar in a statement yesterday said the indiscriminate killing of innocent citizens, our brothers, our sisters, our neighbours can never be justified. It is not only a failure but a gross violation of humanity itself. 

Earlier, the Chief of Defence Staff (CDS), General Christopher Musa, had stated  that the airstrike targeting the Lakurawa insurgents in a community of Silame Local Council, Sokoto State, killing over 10 innocent citizens and wounding others was not only precise but also justified.

He did pointed out while speaking at the 8 Division, Nigeria Army Barracks, Sokoto Thursday at a lunch with troops of Operation FASAN YAMMA, that troops will intensify attacks on enemies of the country until they are entirely routed out and defeated, while stated that airstrike in Sokoto against the Lakurawa terrorist group was not only precise but also justified. Warning the villagers against harbouring terrorists under whatever guise, adding that they do not mean well for the country and must not be allowed to destabilise the nation.

Atiku, who describes the attack as a gross violation of humanity said, “The devastating airstrike that claimed the lives of nearly a dozen innocent civilians and left many others wounded in the peaceful Gidan Sama and Rumtuwa communities in Sokoto State is an outrage that must be condemned in the strongest terms.

“But this tragedy begs the question: What have we truly learnt from the heart-wrenching losses of the past? On December 3, 2023, tens of innocent lives were lost in a brutal airstrike on a religious gathering at Tudun Biri, near Kaduna. How many more lives must be lost before we take action?.

“The indiscriminate killing of innocent citizens – our brothers, our sisters, our neighbours – can never be justified. It is not only a failure but a gross violation of humanity itself.

“When those who are meant to be our partners in the fight against terrorism are instead treated as targets, we are sowing the seeds of further division and anger. We cannot expect them to see a difference between those who protect them and those who harm them when they are caught in the crossfire,” he added.

While calling for a stop to “this tragic cycle of death”, he said, “The only way forward is to learn from the past, to make sure that every life is valued, and to ensure no more families have to mourn the loss of loved ones to senseless violence.”

To the grieving families and the people of Sokoto, he said, “My heart goes out to you. May the souls of the departed rest in eternal peace. Amin.”

He then urged the authorities to learn from the past and avoid recurrence.

title: The Military Airstrike In Sokoto State Was Precise And Justified – CDS
content:
Despite the public outcry of some individuals regarding the military airstrike in Sokoto State that erroneously killed innocent citizens, instead of terrorists,the Chief of Defence Staff (CDS), General Christopher Musa, maintain that the airstrike was not only precise but also justified.

The military warplane was reportedly targeting the Lakurawa insurgents hit a community in Silame Local Council of Sokoto State, killing over 10 innocent citizens and wounding others.

Speaking at the 8 Division, Nigeria Army Barracks, Sokoto Thursday at a lunch with troops of Operation FASAN YAMMA, the CDS reassured that troops will intensify attacks on enemies of the country until they are entirely routed out and defeated, while stated that airstrike in Sokoto against the Lakurawa terrorist group was not only precise but also justified. Warning the villagers against harbouring terrorists under whatever guise, adding that they do not mean well for the country and must not be allowed to destabilise the nation.

‘’From now on and entering 2025, we will give in more. We are going to sacrifice more. We are going to attack more. We will not allow any criminal, whether terrorists, insurgents, bandits, armed robbers, sea pirates or whoever, to destabilise the country. Anybody who crosses the line must face the music.

“Most times, they want to use religion or tribe or sentiments and tell you they are together; they don’t mean well for you. As we see with the Lacurawas, they came in and gave the impression that they were friends, and now they have turned and shown their true colours. We are flushing all of them out, and to all Nigerians and innocent citizens, please do not support them for any reason. Give them logistics, food, money, or go anywhere to stay within your communities. There’s the adage that a friend of a thief is a thief.

‘’Anybody who allows them to stay within him is a legitimate target. I want to make that very clear. We are passionate as we always defend the human rights of every citizen. Still, anybody who allows himself to be used against Nigerians, we are going to go after him.

‘‘So I want to call on any community that is living together with those people, please drive them away or evacuate and leave them because we are coming after them. We will not spare anybody who turns himself into a rat, as the cat will always go to him.

To the troops, “looking ahead, I urge you all to remain steadfast and resolute in your responsibilities. The coming year presents us with an opportunity to make significant progress in overcoming our dear nation’s challenges.

‘’And I want to tell all of us that we will ensure we are steadfast in our approach. We are going to be very robust in our operations.

‘’We appreciate President Bola Ahmed Tinubu because he has approved a lot of enablers so that we can perform our tasks. We will not relent, and all those supporting enemies of the country should be ready. We’ve already started our operations. We’re going to commence and intensify our operations. We want to ensure that nobody is allowed to take any Nigerian hostage wherever he is in the country. It is our duty and task to ensure that every Nigerian can perform his duty freely.

“Together, we must strive to ensure that 2025 is marked by transformative victories in all our operational theatres. Nigerians are all praying for us. Nigerians are all happy with what we are doing and need to do more.

“We will secure the sovereignty of Nigeria and make sure that no elements, no criminal, are allowed to move freely within our territory. I also want to use this to extend our message to our neighbours, Niger Republic, Chad, Cameroon, Benin Republic and Togo, to assure them that Nigeria will not allow anybody, any criminal element, to use its soil to attack any of our neighbouring countries, because we are the same.

“’The only thing we can do is train together, and that is it. We send our officers and soldiers training abroad. They equally send their own to come here for training. They can come here, and we do joint exercises, but no foreign base will be allowed in Nigeria,” the CDS stated.

title: Osimhen: How I Adapted Quickly In Turkey, As Man United Contacts His Representative
content:

title: Pastor Tobi Adegboyega recognize Davido as a gospel musician To Defend Invitation
content:
Flamboyant Nigerian pastor in the United Kingdom, UK, Tobi Adegboyega, during a podcast on the Off The Record podcast while responding to a question on why he invited secular musicians to perform at his recent birthday bash instead of gospel artistes, said, Gospel means good news. Everyone there is a gospel artiste.

Defending David Adeleke aka Davido presence, he said the popular musician is also a gospel artiste pointing out to the ‘Because I stand strong’ single from the artist. While also described Nigerian artist, Zlatan as his son.

He said: “Gospel means good news. Everyone there is a gospel artiste. Davido is a gospel artiste. Have you heard: ‘Because I stand strong?

“What I had then was my friends—friends who are there through thick and thin. Davido told me: ‘I just want to be there and perform for one hour.’ They’re my friends. I didn’t pay any of them. They love me, and I will give my friends platforms.

“If gospel artistes aren’t my friends and are instead joining the bandwagon to criticize me by asking, ‘Is that a church?’ What should I do? Drag them with a rope?

“It’s my friends that will be there. Everyone in that room was my friend. Zlatan is like a son to me; his kids are my kids, and his parents were in my house. So should I now say, ‘Well, because you are not gospel artistes, let me go and look for some gospel artistes who are criticizing me and force them to sing?’

“My friends will always sing at my events, and the next one will be bigger because my circle of friends keeps growing.”
